What Is Digital Media?

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes 'Digital Media'?
options: Internet transmission data wired over limited network
Electronic content that can be transmitted over a computer network
questions.explain: Key: D. Digital media is content in electronic (digital) form that can be stored and transmitted over computer networks.

questions.stem: Which of the following does NOT refer to new media?
options: Feature TV offered over the air broadcast
Democratization of the creation, publishing and distribution of media tools
On demand access to content anytime, anywhere using any digital device
questions.explain: Key: A. Over-the-air broadcast TV is traditional (old) media; the others describe interactive, on-demand new media.

questions.stem: Approximately, for how long have digital media been in existence?
questions.explain: Key: D. Digital media date back to the spread of personal computers in the early 1980s, around 30 years before this paper.

questions.stem: In the early days of digital media, 'advertising' was construed to mean
questions.explain: Key: D. Early digital advertising was seen as agencies creating messages electronically, before websites, smartphones and self-publishing spread.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes 'local content'?
options: Content for people in a certain locality
questions.explain: Key: B. Local content is commonly defined as the expression of the locally owned and adapted knowledge of a community.

questions.stem: In terms of involvement in the digital revolution, the Caribbean Community can be characterized as
questions.explain: Key: D. The Caribbean mostly consumes digital content produced elsewhere rather than creating and exporting its own.

questions.stem: Which of the following is used for media delivery?
questions.explain: Key: A. A mobile phone can receive and play media content; the keyboard and mouse are input devices.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of digital media?
questions.explain: Key: D. Digital media are dynamic and easily changed, connecting people and fostering dialogue rather than producing fixed permanent records.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a pitfall of digital media?
questions.explain: Key: C. Digital media can raise ethical problems, such as privacy and copyright issues, which is a pitfall; boosting a brand is a benefit.

questions.stem: The source of intellectual property can be traced to
questions.explain: Key: B. Intellectual property refers to creations of the mind, such as inventions, designs and artistic works.

questions.stem: Which of the following is MOST likely to raise ethical issues associated with digital media?
options: Stripping of a DRM protected track
Downloading a Linux distribution movie using bittorrent
questions.explain: Key: C. Removing DRM protection bypasses the copyright owner's controls, which raises ethical and legal issues.

questions.stem: Which of the following businesses uses the long-tail business model?
questions.explain: Key: A. iTunes sells huge numbers of niche items in small quantities online, which is the long-tail model.

questions.stem: The open movement does NOT include open
questions.explain: Key: D. Open standards, open access and open source are parts of the open movement; 'open software initiative' is not a recognised part (it is the Open Source Initiative).

questions.stem: Which of the following is a multimedia software tool?
questions.explain: Key: B. Audacity is an audio editing tool; Eclipse is a programming IDE, Word a word processor and Chrome a browser.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are digital media platforms?
I. Satellite
II. Internet
III. 3D art
questions.explain: Key: A. Satellite and the Internet are platforms that deliver digital media; 3D art is a type of content, not a platform.

questions.stem: A 'digital native' is an individual who
options: repairs and maintains computers and servers
was born before the existence of digital technology
was born during the proliferation of digital technology
questions.explain: Key: D. A digital native is someone born into the digital age, growing up with digital technology around them.

questions.stem: A 'digital immigrant' is an individual who
options: has adopted digital technology in later life
has moved away from digital technology
was born before the existence of digital technology
applies the principles of software development
questions.explain: Key: A. A digital immigrant was born before the digital age and adopted digital technology later in life.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the 'digital media ecosystem' concept?
options: A business and corporate communications system
Media based on human communication, and shared electronically
questions.explain: Key: D. The digital media ecosystem is the interconnected system of human communication that is created and shared electronically.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the digital convergence?
options: A global system of computer networks
questions.explain: Key: D. Digital convergence is the merging of different technologies, such as phone, camera and computer, into one device or platform.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the term 'Internet'?
questions.explain: Key: C. The Internet is a global network of interconnected computer networks.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the concept of digital media communication?
questions.explain: Key: D. Digital media communication is interactive and takes place online.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a form of digital media?
questions.explain: Key: C. A feature film show in a cinema is traditional media; e-books, streaming and online services are digital.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT part of the digital media value chain?
questions.explain: Key: A. The value chain covers creating, distributing and managing customers for content; 'single site service' is not a stage.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common work arrangement for digital media practitioners?
questions.explain: Key: A. Digital media practitioners often work in virtual teams, collaborating online from different locations.

questions.stem: Globalization is a process where an increased proportion of
options: engagement takes place through social media
economic, social and cultural activities are carried out across national borders
economic, social and cultural activities are carried out within a country
questions.explain: Key: C. Globalization means more economic, social and cultural activity happens across national borders.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a challenge in the digital media industry?
questions.explain: Key: A. Piracy, the illegal copying and sharing of content, is a major challenge for the digital media industry.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of debt funding?
questions.explain: Key: A. A loan is debt funding because it must be repaid; venture capital and angel investment are equity funding.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a tool for generating ideas?
questions.explain: Key: B. Mind-mapping visually links ideas, making it a useful idea-generation tool.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the purpose of a project proposal?
questions.explain: Key: D. A project proposal introduces and outlines the project to stakeholders; the budget and team are only parts of it.

questions.stem: Which of the following are key aspects of a project proposal?
questions.explain: Key: D. A proposal typically includes a project overview, the target audience and the budget.

questions.stem:
Which of the following sequences describes the creative process?
I. Develop
II. Implement
III. Create
questions.explain: Key: D. Ideas are first created, then developed, and finally implemented.

questions.stem: At which stage in the creative process would a person need to describe the issue to be solved?
questions.explain: Key: B. During analysis the problem is examined and described before ideas are generated.

questions.stem: Which of the following channels of communication does NOT belong to the digital age?
questions.explain: Key: A. Fax is an older, analogue-era technology; blogs, wikis and email are digital-age channels.

questions.stem:
Item 34 refers to the following diagram.

Diagram: seven arrow shapes in a single row, each pointing to the next, left to right: Accept Situation → Analyse → Define → Ideate → Select → Implement → Evaluate.

What type of implementation of the creative process does the diagram illustrate?
questions.explain: Key: B. The stages follow one after another in a straight line with no loop back, so the process is linear.

questions.stem: Which of the following activities is missing from the group: creativity, innovation, concept development?
questions.explain: Key: A. Ideation sits with creativity, innovation and concept development as the idea-generating activities of the creative process.

questions.stem: A writer has developed an outline for a story and has decided to follow it through. What is the next stage in the creative process that should be undertaken?
questions.explain: Key: D. The idea has already been chosen, so the next stage is implementation, actually carrying it out.

questions.stem: Which of the following tasks must be completed prior to the actual making of a digital media product?
questions.explain: Key: C. Pre-production (planning, scripting, storyboarding) must be finished before production begins.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a tool that can be used to edit photographs?
questions.explain: Key: A. Pixlr is an online photo editor; Audacity edits audio and MovieMaker edits video.

questions.stem: Brainstorming, scriptwriting and storyboarding are part of
questions.explain: Key: C. Brainstorming, scripting and storyboarding are planning tasks carried out in pre-production.

questions.stem:
Item 40 refers to the following diagram.

Diagram: titled “Media Pre-Production Process”. A starburst labelled Brainstorm sits at the top. Below it four large downward arrows follow one another: Ideation → Writing → Pre-Visualization → Production Planning, ending in a box that reads: Script breakdown, Create shot list, Make shooting schedule, Make equipment lists. Bars down the sides label related tasks: Develop characters, settings, situations; Research; Develop themes/thesis; Storyboard; Scout locations; Assemble cast and crew.

The diagram shown above is an illustration of
questions.explain: Key: D. All the steps shown happen before filming begins, so the diagram shows the pre-production process.

questions.stem: How many sections are formed when the lines are drawn in relation to the rule of thirds?
questions.explain: Key: C. Two horizontal and two vertical lines divide the frame into nine equal sections.

questions.stem: Which of the following groupings are elements of composition?
options: Rule of thirds and psychology of colours
questions.explain: Key: C. The rule of thirds and lighting both affect how a shot is composed.

questions.stem: A teacher would like her students to recap a particular lesson, ask questions, add comments, add discussion points and post any additional resources. Which digital media tool is most suitable to complete this task?
questions.explain: Key: A. A blog lets the teacher post a recap while students comment, ask questions and share resources in one place.

questions.stem: Which of the following will allow a group of five persons staying at different locations to plan a presentation as a group project for a course?
questions.explain: Key: A. A wiki lets several people in different places edit and build shared content together.

questions.stem: A couple is celebrating their fortieth wedding anniversary. Which of the following will BEST capture all aspects of the years they spent together?
questions.explain: Key: D. Combining audio, photographs and video gives the richest multimedia record of their years together.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the term 'digital media'?
options: Internet transmission data wired over limited network
Electronic content that can be transmitted over a computer network
questions.explain: Key: D. Digital media is content in electronic (digital) form that can be stored and transmitted over computer networks.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes digital convergence?
options: A global system of computer networks
questions.explain: Key: D. Digital convergence is the merging of several communication technologies (text, audio, video, telephony) into one device or platform.

questions.stem: Which of the following phrases BEST describes the term 'Internet'?
questions.explain: Key: A. The Internet is a global network of interconnected computer networks.

questions.stem: Which of the following phrases BEST describes 'local content'?
options: Content for people in a certain locality
questions.explain: Key: D. Local content is the expression of the locally owned and adapted knowledge of a community.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a pitfall of digital media?
questions.explain: Key: C. Ethical problems such as privacy, piracy and misuse of discovered information are a downside of digital media; brand boosting is a benefit.

questions.stem: At which stage of the technology adoption life cycle are individuals more financially stable, have a higher social status and are well educated?
questions.explain: Key: A. In Rogers' adoption model, early adopters are typically well educated, financially secure and of higher social status, and are opinion leaders.

questions.stem: Five persons are planning a presentation as a group project for a course, but are staying at different locations. They should use
questions.explain: Key: A. A wiki lets people in different locations collaboratively create and edit shared content.

questions.stem: John has applied for a job at a digital media company. Which of the following does he need to demonstrate in order to be successful?
questions.explain: Key: C. Digital media is a creative industry, so innovation is the key employability attribute employers seek.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT an element of an elevator pitch?
questions.explain: Key: B. An elevator pitch is brief, clear and catchy; it is not meant to be complete or exhaustive.

questions.stem: Which of the following are major players in the digital media industry?
questions.explain: Key: A. Content producers create the content at the core of the digital media industry.

questions.stem: Which of the following are key aspects of a project proposal?
questions.explain: Key: D. A proposal typically includes a project overview, the target audience and the budget.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a tool for generating ideas?
questions.explain: Key: B. Mind-mapping visually links ideas, making it a useful idea-generation tool.

questions.stem:
Which of the following activities is missing from the group shown below?

Creativity, innovation, concept development
questions.explain: Key: A. Creativity, innovation and concept development are all aspects of ideation, the idea-generating stage.

questions.stem: Which of the following tasks must be completed prior to the actual making of a digital media product?
questions.explain: Key: C. Pre-production (planning, scripting, storyboarding) must be finished before production begins.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a tool that can be used to edit photographs?
questions.explain: Key: A. Pixlr is an online photo editor; Audacity edits audio and MovieMaker edits video.

questions.stem:
