Diagram: titled “Media Pre-Production Process”. A starburst labelled Brainstorm sits at the top. Below it four large downward arrows follow one another: Ideation → Writing → Pre-Visualization → Production Planning, ending in a box that reads: Script breakdown, Create shot list, Make shooting schedule, Make equipment lists. Bars down the sides label related tasks: Develop characters, settings, situations; Research; Develop themes/thesis; Storyboard; Scout locations; Assemble cast and crew.

The diagram shown above is an illustration of
questions.explain: Key: D. All of the steps shown are planning tasks done before shooting, which make up pre-production.

questions.stem: How many sections are formed when imaginary lines are drawn in relation to the rule of thirds?
questions.explain: Key: C. Two horizontal and two vertical lines divide the frame into nine equal sections.

questions.stem: Which of the following groups consists of elements of composition?
options: Rule of thirds and psychology of colours
questions.explain: Key: C. Rule of thirds and lighting are both elements used to compose an image or shot.

questions.stem: The psychology of colours affects exactly how the consumer feels about and views content. Red is one of the primary psychological colors. Which of the following is NOT a positive effect of this colour?
questions.explain: Key: D. Red is stimulating and associated with energy, warmth and strength; calmness is associated with blue.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a term used in digital media?
questions.explain: Key: C. Frame, JPEG and webcast are all common digital media terms; 'isolation' is not.

questions.stem: In digital media, the acronym GIF stands for
questions.explain: Key: C. GIF stands for Graphics Interchange Format, an image file format.

questions.stem: Which of the following operating systems is open source?
questions.explain: Key: B. Android is based on the open-source Linux kernel and released as the Android Open Source Project; the others are proprietary.

questions.stem: The technology used by Betamax for saving is the
questions.explain: Key: D. Betamax was an analogue videocassette format that recorded on magnetic tape.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST defines digital media?
options: Digitized content for use on laptops and tablets only
Digitized content that can be transmitted over the Internet or computer networks
Audio and video content that can be used on computer networks and other platforms
questions.explain: Key: C. Digital media is any digitized content (text, audio, video, graphics) that can be transmitted over the Internet or computer networks.

questions.stem: The development of e-books using Caribbean examination papers and syllabus content is an example of using digital media to
questions.explain: Key: A. Creating e-books from Caribbean exam and syllabus content serves the specific needs of local learners.

questions.stem: A digital media platform is used for the delivery of
options: multimedia files over an Intranet only
video, audio and/or data to multiple networks
streamed and downloadable music for online stores
questions.explain: Key: C. A digital media platform delivers video, audio and data across multiple networks and devices.

questions.stem: On a social networking site, Susan posted a video of herself dancing. Soon, persons started sharing the video link across the Internet. Which ethical issue is now of concern to Susan?
questions.explain: Key: B. Her personal video is spreading beyond the audience she intended, which is a privacy concern.

questions.stem: Which of the following does a patent protect?
questions.explain: Key: A. Patents protect inventions; logos are protected by trademarks.

questions.stem: Which of the following does NOT present an ethical issue in the field of digital media?
options: John sharing a video he shot and edited with his friends
John copying a commercial CD he borrowed from his friend
John selling a popular movie that he downloaded from YouTube
John downloading an expensive video editing suite from a file sharing site
questions.explain: Key: A. Sharing his own original video raises no ethical issue; the others involve copyright infringement or piracy.

questions.stem: Jill is writing a new book and wants the final product to be in electronic format. Which of the following digital media businesses will be MOST suitable for doing this?
questions.explain: Key: C. Interactive media firms produce digital and interactive products such as e-books.

questions.stem: Your teacher has created a very interesting lesson plan and has decided she would like to share with other teachers by placing it on her blog. This lesson plan can be classified as
questions.explain: Key: B. Teaching materials freely shared for others to use are open educational resources (OER).

questions.stem: Which of the following tools is MOST appropriate for completing a wedding video?
questions.explain: Key: C. Movie Maker is a video editor; Picasa is for photos, Ardour for audio and Dreamweaver for websites.

questions.stem: Which of the following tools may be used in the preparation of a printable photo album?
questions.explain: Key: A. Picasa organises and edits photos and can create printable collages and albums; Audacity and Wavosaur are audio editors.

questions.stem: The phrase ‘pervasiveness of technology’ refers to
options: the limited use of digital technology in some societies
the result of ‘throwing’ too much technology at a problem
the use of technology as a tool for misconduct in some societies
technology being widely available in almost every aspect of daily life
questions.explain: Key: D. Pervasive means spread throughout, so technology is present in almost every part of daily life.

questions.stem: A digital native can be described as a person who
options: uses the Internet to complete all tasks
uses all the social networks for communicating
has grown up using technology as a way of communicating with others
has adapted to the digital world using technology to communicate with others
questions.explain: Key: C. Digital natives grew up with digital technology; those who adapted later are digital immigrants.

questions.stem: A person who is NOT part of the digital generation is MOST likely to
options: purchase a book online from Amazon
questions.explain: Key: A. Paying bills in person is a non-digital habit; the other options rely on online services.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the digital media environment?
options: The availability of the Internet to do research
The use of mobile phones to complete daily tasks
The use of desktops and laptops to connect online and communicate
The proliferation of devices people use to consume content at home, at work and on the go
questions.explain: Key: D. The digital media environment is the wide range of devices people use to consume content everywhere, not one device or task.

questions.stem: Which of the following devices is gaining prominence within the digital media ecosystem?
questions.explain: Key: D. Mobile phones were already established. Wearables such as smartwatches and fitness bands were the growing category.

questions.stem:
This item refers to the following value chain.

Diagram: five boxes joined by arrows, left to right: Content Creation → Aggregation & Publishing → Distribution (Fixed & Mobile) → Customer Environment → Stakeholder.

The stakeholder is MOST likely the
questions.explain: Key: A. The chain flows from creation through distribution to the customer environment, so the end stakeholder who consumes the content is the customer.

questions.stem: The owner of Jack’s Tyre Shop communicates with his suppliers in another territory using a computer with a microphone and a webcam connected to the Internet. Which of the following forms of communication uses ALL these technologies?
questions.explain: Key: D. Videoconferencing uses a webcam, microphone and Internet connection for live audio and video meetings.

questions.stem: A digitally connected team comprising members located in three different countries, completed a project. This model of working is known as
questions.explain: Key: C. Telecommuting is working remotely through digital connections instead of being in a shared workplace.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a MAJOR challenge faced by the digital media industry in the Caribbean landscape?
questions.explain: Key: D. A shortage of skilled digital media workers is a key regional challenge to growing the industry.

questions.stem: Which of the following is one of the MAJOR technical challenges that businesses may face in managing their digital media?
questions.explain: Key: B. Digital media files are large and grow quickly, so backing them up reliably is a major technical challenge.

questions.stem: John’s restaurant is located in a town that has a large population of digital immigrants. The manager notices that sales have dropped and is considering how to address this. Which of the following is the BEST method to advertise the restaurant’s goods to the community?
questions.explain: Key: B. Digital immigrants are less at home online but commonly use basic mobile features, so text messages reach them most directly.

questions.stem: Paul decides to open a business that designs websites; however, he needs to seek financing. He is required to provide a detailed business plan, along with any collateral, expected cash flow statement and asset liquidity position to the financial institution. What type of financing is Paul seeking?
questions.explain: Key: A. Asking for collateral and cash flow statements is typical of a bank loan, which is debt financing.

questions.stem: Which of the following may BEST enhance employability?
questions.explain: Key: D. A personal portfolio shows employers evidence of a digital media worker's skills and past work.

questions.stem:
Item 28 refers to the following diagram.

Diagram: four small cloud shapes down the left side. From each cloud, three arrows lead to three blank rectangular boxes on the right, making twelve empty boxes in all.

The diagram can be used to complete a
questions.explain: Key: D. Each starting idea branches to several linked words, which is the pattern of a word association exercise. There is no single central topic, as a mind map would have.

questions.stem: Concept formulation is important because it provides
options: a set of materials to formulate and display ideas
an approach for forming relationships between concepts
a way to make connections and form relationships among peers
an opportunity to explore ideas by making connections between items of information
questions.explain: Key: D. Concept formulation lets you explore ideas by connecting pieces of information to build a concept.

questions.stem:
Oral presentation skills are important in the world of digital media because they
I. can help to communicate complex concepts
II. can enhance selling skills
III. allow for visual representation of data
questions.explain: Key: B. Good oral skills help explain complex ideas and sell or pitch them; visual representation of data comes from visual aids, not speaking.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the complete creative process?
options: Designing a solution for two related problems
Taking a problem through to an implemented solution
Taking a problem through to a solution being designed
Taking a solution and retracing how the problem was solved
questions.explain: Key: B. The complete creative process runs from accepting the problem all the way to implementing (and evaluating) the solution.

questions.stem: During which stage of the creative process is the individual required to take time to study the problem at hand and how it relates to its various components?
questions.explain: Key: A. Analysis means studying the problem and how its parts relate.

questions.stem: An entrepreneur is applying the creative process to solve a problem. At which point in the process will he do a mind mapping chart?
questions.explain: Key: C. Mind mapping is an idea-generation technique, so it is used in the ideation stage.

questions.stem: After studying and defining the problem, the next step in the creative process will be to
questions.explain: Key: B. After analysis and definition comes ideation, which is generating ideas.

questions.stem:
Item 35 refers to the following diagram.

Diagram: five circles joined by single lines in a zigzag chain, from bottom to top: Create the problem — Create the solution context — Create solutions — Develop details — Use and give feedback. There are no loops and no branches.

The diagram illustrates the stages in a creative process. The methodology illustrated in the diagram is
questions.explain: Key: A. The stages follow one after another in a single line with no return path or branches, so the method is linear.

questions.stem: A group, while working on a project, discusses the problem and records all ideas that come to mind. This is known as
questions.explain: Key: C. Recording every idea that comes to mind without judging it is brainstorming.

questions.stem: A software team is designing a website for a retail clothing store. Which of the following is an important factor when developing the site?
questions.explain: Key: B. Many shoppers browse on phones and tablets, so the site must work well on mobile devices generally, not just one platform.

questions.stem: Pre-production relating to video refers to
options: all tasks associated with the film
tasks that must be completed during filming
tasks that must be completed before filming
tasks that must be completed after filming
questions.explain: Key: C. Pre-production is all the planning done before filming starts, such as scripting, storyboarding and scheduling.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a core element in pre-production?
questions.explain: Key: C. Location scouting is a core pre-production task done before shooting begins.

questions.stem: Which of the following should be considered when designing a website to assist toddlers in identifying different objects?
questions.explain: Key: D. Colour strongly affects young children's attention and recognition, so colour psychology is key for a toddler audience.

questions.stem: Juanita has made a video of her baby brother, and would like to delete a part of the video that was included because she forgot to turn off the recording. Which of the following would be BEST for Juanita to use to accomplish this?
questions.explain: Key: B. iMovie is a video editor that can trim unwanted footage; the other tools edit photos or audio.

questions.stem: A client has asked you to ensure that an advertisement is seen mostly by persons between the ages of 19 and 21. What type of targeting would need to be used?
questions.explain: Key: D. Targeting by age is demographic targeting.

questions.stem: Which of the following can be used for organizing information between groups of people?
questions.explain: Key: B. A wiki lets many users work together to add, edit and organise shared information.

questions.stem: Julie started an assignment in the computer lab at school with the intention of continuing at home. Although she did not have her flash drive, she was still able to access the document at home. Which of the following did Julie MOST likely use to save her document?
questions.explain: Key: D. Cloud storage keeps files online so they can be opened from any connected device.

questions.stem: Which of the following formats is BEST for creating a video of a school’s graduation ceremony?
questions.explain: Key: A. MPEG-2 is a video format; JPEG and GIF are image formats and WAV is audio.

questions.stem: Software that can be used and modified from its original source and sold to other users is BEST described as open
questions.explain: Key: B. Open source software has source code that anyone may use, modify and redistribute, including selling it.

questions.stem: In digital media, the acronym GIF stands for
questions.explain: Key: D. GIF stands for Graphics Interchange Format, an image file format.

questions.stem: John wants to reduce the size of his audio file before putting it on his website. Which of the following is MOST useful for John’s situation?
questions.explain: Key: C. Compression makes a file smaller so it loads and streams faster on the web.

questions.stem: Which of the following icons represents the Creative Commons licensing system?
options: [Icon: a person figure in a circle]
[Icon: a crossed-out dollar sign in a circle]
[Icon: a circular arrow in a circle]
questions.explain: Key: D. The 'cc' in a circle is the main Creative Commons logo; the other icons stand for individual licence conditions (Attribution, NonCommercial, ShareAlike).

questions.stem: On a social networking site, Susan posted a video of herself dancing. Soon, persons started sharing the video link across the Internet. Which of the following ethical issues should be of concern to Susan?
questions.explain: Key: B. Her personal video is spreading beyond the audience she intended, which is a privacy concern.

questions.stem: A patent is a set of exclusive rights that protects
questions.explain: Key: B. Patents protect inventions, not bare ideas; logos are protected by trademarks.

questions.stem:
Arrange the items below to represent the CORRECT sequence of creating a digital video.
I. Editing
II. Production
III. Storyboarding
questions.explain: Key: D. Storyboarding is pre-production, then the footage is shot (production), then it is edited (post-production).

questions.stem: Which of the following tools is associated with photo editing?
questions.explain: Key: C. LiveQuartz is an image and photo editor; YouTube is video sharing, Audacity edits audio and Aptana Studio is a web IDE.

questions.stem: Which of the following activities could be considered a cybercrime?
options: Saving customer data to a thumb drive
Using a free software to develop an app
questions.explain: Key: B. Intercepting other people's communications without authorisation is illegal interception, a cybercrime.

questions.stem: Spencer downloaded the latest calypso music and ‘burnt’ copies of CDs to sell to his friends. What ethical issue would his action raise?
questions.explain: Key: D. Copying and selling music without the rights holder's permission is copyright infringement (piracy).

questions.stem: The phrase ‘pervasiveness of technology’ refers to the
options: limited use of digital technology in some societies
result of ‘throwing’ too much technology at a problem
use of technology as a tool for misconduct in some societies
availability of technology in almost every aspect of daily life
questions.explain: Key: D. Pervasive means spread throughout, so technology is present in almost every part of daily life.

questions.stem:
Using the following list of elements, what is the MOST likely common sequence for pitching a project?
I. Proposal
II. Problem
III. Conclusion
questions.explain: Key: C. A pitch first states the problem, then proposes the solution, then concludes.

questions.stem: After brainstorming and having identified her target audience, Anika combined various media elements to create a layout for her new website. Which of the following BEST describes the phase she has just completed?
questions.explain: Key: D. Combining actual media elements into a page layout is interface design; a wireframe is only a bare skeleton without media.

questions.stem: Richard is making a presentation to young adults on the topic of ‘Digital media’. Which of the following visual aids is LEAST likely to be suitable for this presentation?
questions.explain: Key: C. A wireframe is a bare planning sketch, not an engaging visual aid; video, animation and interactive slides suit a young audience.

questions.stem: The digital media ecosystem can BEST be described as the
options: environment in which digital media exists
IT industry and the persons that support digital media
components of digital media working together continuously
components of digital media and the infrastructure that supports it
questions.explain: Key: D. The ecosystem includes both the parts of digital media (content, devices, users) and the infrastructure that supports them.

questions.stem: Which of the following terms BEST describes the emergence of worldwide markets?
questions.explain: Key: B. Globalization is the integration of national economies into worldwide markets.

questions.stem: John wants to seek funding for his business proposal but the banking sector does not want to take the risks to provide funding. Which of the following is the BEST source of funding for his business proposal?
questions.explain: Key: C. Crowdfunding raises small amounts from many people online, which avoids relying on risk-averse lenders.

questions.stem: The Digital Media Value Chain describes
questions.explain: Key: A. A value chain shows how value is added (enhanced) at each stage as content moves from creation to the customer.

questions.stem: Paul decides to open a business that designs websites; however, he needs to seek financing. He is required to provide a detailed business plan, along with collateral, expected cash flow statement and asset liquidity position to the financial institution. What type of financing is Paul seeking?
questions.explain: Key: A. Asking for collateral and cash flow statements is typical of a bank loan, which is debt financing.

questions.stem: Which of the following activities BEST describes the process of brainstorming?
options: Testing the effectiveness of a prototype
Drawing a diagram to represent ideas linked to a central keyword
questions.explain: Key: D. Brainstorming generates and links many ideas around a central topic, often drawn as a diagram. The other options belong to other stages.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a method of idea generation?
questions.explain: Key: C. Free writing, brainstorming and word association are standard idea-generation techniques; 'digital mapping' is not (mind mapping is).

questions.stem: Concept formulation is important because it provides
options: a set of materials to prepare and display ideas
an approach for forming relationships between concepts
a way to make connections and form relationships among peers
an opportunity to explore ideas by making connections between items of information
questions.explain: Key: D. Concept formulation lets you explore ideas by connecting pieces of information to build a concept.

questions.stem:
Oral presentation skills are important in the world of digital media because they
I. can enhance marketing skills
II. allow for visual representation of data
III. can help to communicate complex concepts
questions.explain: Key: C. Good oral skills help market ideas and explain complex concepts; visual representation of data comes from visual aids, not speaking.

questions.stem: An entrepreneur is applying the creative process to solve a problem. At which point in the process should he do a mind-mapping chart?
questions.explain: Key: A. Mind mapping is an idea-generation technique, so it is used in the ideation stage.

questions.stem: After studying and defining the problem, the next step in the creative process is to
questions.explain: Key: B. After analysis and definition comes ideation, which is generating ideas.

questions.stem:
This item refers to the following diagram which shows an approach to the creative process.

Diagram: from Accept situation two arrows lead off. The upper path goes to Analysis, which splits into Ideate and Define. The lower path goes to Define, which splits into Ideate and Re-Analyze; Re-Analyze leads to another Ideate. Every one of these paths ends at Select. Select leads to Implement, which splits into Evaluate and Re-Analyze, and Re-Analyze also points to Evaluate.

Which of the following terms BEST describes this approach?
questions.explain: Key: D. The process splits into several alternative paths that later rejoin, so it is a branched approach.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a core preproduction task when doing digital video production?
questions.explain: Key: C. Visual effects are added in post-production; logistics, budgeting and storyboarding are done before filming.

questions.stem: A software team is designing a website for a retail clothing store. Which of the following is an important factor to be considered?
questions.explain: Key: C. Many shoppers browse on phones and tablets, so the site must work well on mobile devices generally, not just one platform.

questions.stem: The arrangement of elements within a user interface or layout is called
questions.explain: Key: B. Composition is the overall arrangement of visual elements in a layout.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT considered part of the five-step approach to the ideation process in developing an inventive solution?
questions.explain: Key: B. Defining the problem, generating ideas and evaluating them are core ideation steps; validation is not part of this model.

questions.stem: During which of the following phases of producing a gaming website would JavaScript be added?
questions.explain: Key: D. Code such as JavaScript is written and added when the planned design is built, which is the implementation phase.

questions.stem: Sunil is editing a video, the final output will be posted on the Internet. Which of the following formats would BEST allow for immediate use on the web?
questions.explain: Key: A. FLV (Flash Video) was designed for streaming video on the web. MPEG-4 is also widely used online, which makes this item debatable.

questions.stem: What type of targeting should be used to ensure that an advertisement is seen mostly by persons between the ages of 19 and 21?
questions.explain: Key: D. Targeting by age is demographic targeting.

questions.stem:
A video was edited using a video editing suite. In which of the following ways may it be shared?
I. Exported as an FLV file
II. Exported as a WAV file
III. Uploaded online to YouTube
questions.explain: Key: B. FLV is a video format and YouTube hosts video; WAV is audio only and cannot hold the video.

questions.stem:
Which of the following gives the correct sequence for pitching a project?
I. Proposal
II. Problem
III. Conclusion
questions.explain: Key: C. A pitch first states the problem, then presents the proposed solution, and ends with a conclusion.

questions.stem: The term 'new media' refers to the use of technologies to
options: Ensure that content is up to date
questions.explain: Key: B. New media describes digital, often interactive, technologies used to communicate content to an audience.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT considered a form of digital communication?
questions.explain: Key: A. Traditional fax transmits scanned documents as analogue signals over telephone lines, unlike Skype, e-mail and mobile phones.

questions.stem: Which of the following does NOT present an ethical issue in the field of digital media?
options: John sharing a video he shot and edited with his friends
Camille copying a commercial CD she borrowed from her friend
Simone selling a popular movie that she downloaded from YouTube
Rayman downloading an expensive video editing suite from a file sharing site
questions.explain: Key: A. John owns the video he created, so sharing it raises no copyright or ethical problem; the others involve copying or distributing others' work.

questions.stem:
Michael has developed a mobile app that allows users to enter their gender and shoe size; it then searches for appropriate shoes at two major online retailers.
Which of the following would NOT have been a necessary step in the process of developing this mobile app?
options: Developing a story board and a shot list
Obtaining a price list from a local shoe retailer
Doing a survey to determine the appropriateness of the app
Obtaining a list of all the possible shoe sizes from a local shoe retailer
questions.explain: Key: B. The app only searches two online retailers, so a local retailer’s price list plays no part in developing it.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the complete creative process?
options: Designing a solution for two related problems
Taking a problem through to an implemented solution
Taking a problem through to a solution being designed
Designing a solution and testing how the problem is to be solved
questions.explain: Key: B. The full creative process runs from accepting and defining a problem all the way to implementing (and evaluating) a solution.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a skill needed to enhance entrepreneurship in the digital media industry?
questions.explain: Key: A. Entrepreneurship depends on learning, a portfolio and marketing ideas; programming is a technical skill, not an entrepreneurial one.

questions.stem: Which of the following is likely to occur MORE frequently given the increased use of the Internet and digital tools?
questions.explain: Key: D. Wider use of the Internet and digital tools brings more ethical questions such as privacy, piracy and plagiarism.

questions.stem: Which of the following is necessary in clearly defining a problem?
questions.explain: Key: B. Breaking a problem into its parts clarifies exactly what must be solved, which is the purpose of the define stage.

questions.stem: A production team is considering using existing material such as photographs, audio and graphics sourced from the Internet. Which of the following intellectual property issues should the team be concerned with?
questions.explain: Key: C. Photographs, audio and graphics are creative works protected by copyright, so permission or licensing is needed.

questions.stem:
Which of the following statements are TRUE about venture capitalists?
I. They only fund large business
II. They provide equity for businesses
III. They expect high returns on their investments
questions.explain: Key: C. Venture capitalists invest equity, often in small high-growth start-ups, and expect high returns for the risk they take.

questions.stem: When measuring environmental challenges and opportunities, context is usually measured as
questions.explain: Key: A. Environmental scanning considers the context at local and global levels.

questions.stem: Camille was born in 2013 and is referred to as a digital native because
options: Persons born after the year 2000 all have digital birth certificates
Her parents are likely young enough to have grown up in the digital age
Being born after the year 2010, her medical records are digitally managed
She was born during or after the general introduction of digital technology
questions.explain: Key: D. A digital native is someone who grew up during or after the widespread introduction of digital technology.

questions.stem: Anila is designing an interactive map for her school’s website and wants to highlight multiple locations on the map. Which of the following software would be BEST for implementing the map?
questions.explain: Key: D. Online mapping tools such as Google My Maps let you mark multiple locations on an interactive map for a website.

questions.stem: A digital media platform is a digitized platform used for
options: Sharing data openly among students and teachers
Storing different types of data within a closed network
Delivering audio, video and data across multiple networks
questions.explain: Key: D. Digital media platforms exist to deliver audio, video and data to users across multiple networks.

questions.stem: James printed a copy of his friend's school-based assessment and submitted it to his teacher as his own. Which of the following ethical issues would arise from his action?
questions.explain: Key: C. Presenting someone else's work as your own is plagiarism.

questions.stem:
Michael has developed a mobile app that allows users to enter their gender and shoe size; it then searches for appropriate shoes at two major online retailers.
Which of the following would have been the MOST important consideration when designing this mobile app?
options: Making the size of the app as big as possible
Including an icon for different types of phones
Including a tool that detects geographical location
Ensuring that it works with different screen sizes
questions.explain: Key: D. Mobile apps run on many devices, so responsive design for different screen sizes is the key consideration.

questions.stem:
An effects factory will MOST likely work on
I. Mobile apps
II. Digital video
III. Digital audio
questions.explain: Key: B. An effects factory (visual effects studio) mainly produces visual effects for film and digital video.

questions.stem:
Item 21 refers to the following diagram.

Diagram: from Accept situation two arrows lead off. The upper path goes to Analysis, which splits into Ideate and Define. The lower path goes to Define, which splits into Ideate and Re-Analyze; Re-Analyze leads to another Ideate. Every one of these paths ends at Select. Select leads to Implement, which splits into Evaluate and Re-Analyze, and Re-Analyze also points to Evaluate.

Which of the following terms BEST describes the approach to the creative process shown in the diagram above?
questions.explain: Key: D. The process splits into alternative paths that later rejoin, which is a branched approach.

questions.stem: Which of the following stages requires understanding of the problem in the Universal Traveler model of the creative process?
questions.explain: Key: B. In the Universal Traveler model, the Analysis stage gathers facts to understand the problem.

questions.stem:
Item 23 refers to the following value chain.

Diagram: five boxes joined by arrows, left to right: Content Creation → Aggregation & Publishing → Distribution (Fixed & Mobile) → Customer Environment → Stakeholder.

The stakeholder, in the diagram above, is MOST likely the
questions.explain: Key: A. The chain ends with content reaching the customer's environment, so the final stakeholder is the customer who consumes the content.

questions.stem: Storyboard Pro, Animoto and Wavepad are all
questions.explain: Key: B. They cover storyboarding, video creation and audio editing, so the only common category is digital media tools.

questions.stem: Historically Web 2.0 tends to refer to a time in the history of the Internet when
options: Web 1.0 websites started to become less popular
Websites began to adopt HTML5 and Javascript
The option for users to add or modify information became more prevalent
A new version of the web was released by the World Wide Web Consortium
questions.explain: Key: C. Web 2.0 describes the shift to user-generated content and interaction, such as blogs, wikis and social media.

questions.stem: Which of the following working models is also referred to as 'nomadic' working?
questions.explain: Key: C. Nomadic or virtual working means working from any location using mobile technology, not tied to a fixed office.

questions.stem: The term 'bandwidth' refers to
options: The download speed of a connection
The number of IP addresses present in a network
The transmission capacity of a communication line
questions.explain: Key: D. Bandwidth is the maximum data transmission capacity of a communication channel.

questions.stem: The process of idea generation encourages
questions.explain: Key: C. Idea generation (brainstorming) defers judgement and encourages wild, outlandish ideas to maximise options.

questions.stem: A collection of systems that is used to protect the copyright of electronic media is referred to as a
questions.explain: Key: C. Digital Rights Management (DRM) systems control access to and copying of copyrighted digital media.

questions.stem: Which of the following activities can be considered a cybercrime?
options: Saving customer data to a thumb drive
Using a free software to develop an app
questions.explain: Key: B. Intercepting other people's communications without authorisation is an illegal computer-related crime.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an important part of the planning process when preparing to build a website?
questions.explain: Key: A. A wireframe maps out the page layout and structure during website planning, before design and building.

questions.stem: Which of the following represents a step in the creation stage of a website?
questions.explain: Key: B. Adding content is done while building the site; a site map is planned earlier, and exporting and distribution come later.

questions.stem: Audio editing can be done using
questions.explain: Key: D. GoldWave is an audio editor; GIMP edits images, iTunes plays media and Animoto makes videos.

questions.stem: The digital media ecosystem can BEST be described as the
options: Environment in which digital media exists
IT industry and the persons who support digital media
Components of digital media working together continuously
Components of digital media and the infrastructure that supports them
questions.explain: Key: D. The digital media ecosystem includes the content and components of digital media together with the infrastructure that supports and delivers them.

questions.stem:
Susan posted a video of herself dancing on a social networking site. Immediately after, persons started sharing the video link across the Internet.
Which of the following ethical issues should Susan have considered before posting?
questions.explain: Key: B. Once posted, personal content can spread beyond her control, so she should have considered her privacy.

questions.stem: Which of the following is considered a MAJOR benefit of telecommuting?
questions.explain: Key: D. Working from home removes the daily commute, saving travel cost and time.

questions.stem: Omar wants to seek funding for his business proposal. The banking sector does not want to take the risk of providing funding. What is the BEST alternative source of funding for his business proposal?
questions.explain: Key: C. Crowdfunding raises money from many people online without needing a lender to accept the risk.

questions.stem: A storyboard is created
options: Immediately after a screenplay is written
questions.explain: Key: A. A storyboard is a pre-production tool used to plan shots before filming begins.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are components of a project proposal?
I. Objectives
II. Project duration
III. Expected results
questions.explain: Key: D. A project proposal states its objectives, timeline and expected outcomes.

questions.stem:
Technological advances in digital media have brought opportunities as well as challenges in the delivery of innovative content experiences. These challenges may include the
I. Increasing cost of maintaining the latest technology
II. Complexity of continually adapting to the latest technology
III. Difficulty of disposing of old technology
questions.explain: Key: D. Keeping up with technology raises costs, demands constant adaptation and creates e-waste, so all three are challenges.

questions.stem: Historically, Web 2.0 tends to refer to a time in the history of the Internet when
options: Web 1.0 websites started to become less popular
websites began to adopt HTML5 and JavaScript
a new version of the web was released by the World Wide Web consortium
interaction and ability for users to add or modify information became more important
questions.explain: Key: D. Web 2.0 describes the shift to a participatory web where users create, share and modify content; it was not a formal release by the W3C.

questions.stem: John wants to reduce the size of his audio file before putting it on his website. Which of the following would be MOST useful in reducing the size of the file?
questions.explain: Key: C. Compression removes redundant or less important data so the file takes up less storage space.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an open source operating system?
questions.explain: Key: B. Android is built on the open source Android Open Source Project and Linux kernel; the others are proprietary.

questions.stem: A collection of systems used to protect the copyrights of electronic media is referred to as
questions.explain: Key: C. Digital rights management (DRM) is the set of technologies used to control access to and copying of copyrighted digital content.

questions.stem: Which of the following types of licenses allows an author to give people the right to use, share and build upon his work?
questions.explain: Key: D. Creative Commons licences let creators grant the public permission to use, share and build on their work under stated conditions.

questions.stem: The development of e-books using Caribbean Examinations Council papers and syllabus content is an example of using digital media to
questions.explain: Key: A. E-books built from CXC syllabus content serve the specific needs of Caribbean students, which is addressing local needs.

questions.stem: Which of the following skills may NOT be needed to enhance entrepreneurship in the digital media industry?
questions.explain: Key: A. Continuous learning, a portfolio and marketing ability are core entrepreneurial skills, while programming is a technical skill not every digital media entrepreneur needs.

questions.stem:
Steven wants to start a music production business that requires $100 000 to start up. He has $50 000 in savings and his brother invests $25 000. He then acquires a $25 000 loan from the bank to make up the total amount.
This type of funding can be BEST described as
questions.explain: Key: C. The savings and his brother's investment are equity, while the bank loan is debt, so the funding is a mix of both.

questions.stem: Which of the following is considered a MAJOR benefit of telecommuting?
questions.explain: Key: D. Working from home removes the daily commute, so the most direct benefit is reduced travel cost.

questions.stem:
Which of the following statements are TRUE about venture capitalists?
I. They only fund large businesses.
II. They provide equity for businesses.
III. They expect high returns on their investments.
questions.explain: Key: C. Venture capitalists invest money in exchange for equity and expect high returns; they often fund small, high-growth start-ups rather than only large businesses.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are the parts of a project proposal?
I. Objectives
II. Project duration
III. Expected results
questions.explain: Key: D. A project proposal sets out its objectives, the timeline or duration, and the expected results or outcomes.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a MAJOR challenge faced by the digital media industry in the Caribbean?
questions.explain: Key: D. The Caribbean digital media industry is limited by a shortage of trained, skilled practitioners.

questions.stem: John wants to seek funding for his business proposal but the banking sector does not want to take the risks to provide funding. Which of the following is the BEST source of funding for his business proposal?
questions.explain: Key: C. Crowdfunding raises small amounts from many people online, so it does not depend on a lender or single investor accepting the risk.

questions.stem: Paul decides to open a business that designs websites; however, he needs to seek financing. The financial institution requires him to provide a detailed business plan, an expected cash flow statement, an asset liquidity position, and collateral. What type of financing is Paul seeking?
questions.explain: Key: A. Collateral and cash-flow evidence are required when borrowing a loan, which is debt financing.

questions.stem:
Michael has developed a mobile application that allows users to search for appropriate shoes at two major online retailers by entering their gender and shoe size.

Which of the following would NOT be a necessary step in the process of developing this application?
options: Developing a storyboard and a shot list
Obtaining a price list from a local shoe retailer
Doing a survey to determine the appropriateness of the app
Obtaining a list of all the possible shoe sizes from a local shoe retailer
questions.explain: Key: B. The app only searches two online retailers, so a local retailer’s price list plays no part in developing it.

questions.stem: When creating a video of a school's graduation ceremony to be sold to students, which of the following is the BEST format for the final product?
questions.explain: Key: A. MPEG-2 is a video format (used for DVDs); JPEG and GIF are image formats and WAV is audio.

questions.stem: Which of the following techniques allows a user to efficiently share multiple files as a single file across digital platforms?
questions.explain: Key: D. Compression tools such as ZIP bundle many files into one smaller archive for easy sharing.

questions.stem: A collection of systems used to protect the copyrights of electronic media is referred to as
questions.explain: Key: C. Digital rights management (DRM) is the set of technologies used to control access to and copying of copyrighted digital content.

questions.stem:
This item refers to the drawing canvas shown below.

Picture: a drawing program window with a toolbar of drawing tools down the left side. On the grid canvas is a colour cartoon of a boy in a red helmet, orange shirt and blue jeans doing a trick on a green skateboard.

Max is contracted by Skaters International to create an animated logo for use in their marketing campaign using social media marketing. Which of the following describes scanned art work which is further edited and finalized using artistic software?
questions.explain: Key: C. Hand-made art that is scanned into a computer and then refined with software is digitized artwork.

questions.stem:
This item refers to the picture below.

Picture: a photograph of a real street with buildings and parked cars. In front of the scene a hand holds up a torn piece of paper with a pencil line drawing of a bus on it. The drawing lines up with the street behind it, so the sketch and the photograph blend into one image.

The combination of emerging technologies, such as robotics, physical science, art and other studies, which produce graphics that can entail gestures and speech, can be classified as
questions.explain: Key: D. Combining several technologies and disciplines, like mixing a drawing with a photograph, produces hybrid graphics.

questions.stem: Which of the following file types CANNOT be used as a video format?
questions.explain: Key: B. PNG is a still image format; AVI, MPG and WMV are video formats.

questions.stem: Which of the following creation techniques use geometrical primitives such as points, curves, lines and shapes to produce images in computer graphics?
questions.explain: Key: A. Vector graphics are defined mathematically by points, lines, curves and shapes, so they scale without losing quality.

questions.stem: Which of the following does NOT present an ethical issue in the field of digital media?
options: John sharing a video he shot and edited with his friends.
John copying a commercial CD he borrowed from his friend.
John selling a popular movie that he downloaded from YouTube.
John downloading an expensive video editing suite from a file sharing site.
questions.explain: Key: A. Sharing his own original video raises no ethical issue; the others involve copyright infringement or piracy.

questions.stem: When one does a preliminary version of a film by producing successive sections using storyboard and then add a sound track, this is referred to as
questions.explain: Key: A. An animatic is a storyboard played in sequence with a soundtrack to preview the timing of a film.

questions.stem: Which of the following processes must be completed immediately before an end user is able to purchase a new device?
questions.explain: Key: C. After a device is created and produced, it must be distributed to retailers before end users can buy it.

questions.stem: Brainstorming is BEST for idea
questions.explain: Key: C. Brainstorming is a technique for generating many ideas quickly without judging them.

questions.stem: How does globalization impact the digital media expansion?
questions.explain: Key: C. Globalization opens worldwide markets and audiences, which speeds up the growth of digital media.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are parts of a project proposal?
I. Objectives
II. Project duration
III. Expected results
questions.explain: Key: D. A project proposal sets out its objectives, the duration and the expected results.

questions.stem: Which of the following persons is MOST likely a digital native?
questions.explain: Key: C. A digital native grew up surrounded by digital technology, which fits the youngest person.

questions.stem: As a digital media practitioner, which of the following may BEST enhance employability?
questions.explain: Key: D. A personal portfolio shows employers real evidence of a digital media practitioner's skills and work.

questions.stem:
Oral presentation skills are important in the world of digital media because they
I. can enhance marketing skills
II. allow for visual representation of data
III. can help to communicate complex concepts
questions.explain: Key: B. Strong oral presentation helps sell ideas and explain complex concepts; visual representation of data comes from visuals, not speaking skills.

questions.stem: Which of the following elements is MOST important for enhancing entrepreneurial skills?
questions.explain: Key: A. Skills improve through ongoing learning; finance and certification do not in themselves build entrepreneurial skill.

questions.stem: When using a PowerPoint file for a public presentation, which of the following describes the background for the slides?
options: Calming artistic photo of a landscape
Any type of photo related to the content
Exciting and colorful image that keeps attention
questions.explain: Key: A. A simple colour scheme keeps text readable and does not distract the audience from the content.

questions.stem: Which of the following steps is first in the creative process?
questions.explain: Key: C. The creative process begins with accepting the situation (the problem) before analysing it.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are methods of implementing the creative process?
I. Linear
II. Square
III. Cyclic
questions.explain: Key: B. The creative process can be followed in a linear or cyclic way; square is not a recognised approach.

questions.stem: What type of targeting should be used to ensure that an advertisement is seen mostly by persons between the ages of 18 and 21?
questions.explain: Key: D. Age is a demographic characteristic, so demographic targeting is used.

questions.stem:
Diagram: a cycle of six circles linked by arrows: product → optimize → markets → research → strategy → biz dev → back to product. In the middle are four coloured blocks labelled media, technology, audience and impact.

At what stage of the production process will the above chart/graph/illustration be referred to?
options: Both in Pre-Production, and Post Production
questions.explain: Key: D. The cycle covers planning (research, strategy) and evaluating results (optimize, markets), so it is used both in pre-production and post-production.

questions.stem: When text is to be added to video production, this is done sometimes at the end of the production, though it can be done at other points. When the text is added to the end of the production of a video, this is referred to as:
questions.explain: Key: D. Text at the end of a video listing the people involved is called the credits.

questions.stem:
Picture: two small toolbar icons from a video editing program. The first shows a bar with a vertical marker separating a filled (blue) section from an empty section. The second shows a filled (blue) section held between two vertical markers, with empty sections outside them.

The above icons are used to carry out what important task in video editing?
options: Remove excess sound from a production
Remove sections of video or sound that is not required for production
Add extra video footage to a production being created in video editing
Modify sections of a video before finalising production
questions.explain: Key: B. Split and trim tools cut clips so unwanted portions of video or sound can be removed.

questions.stem:
Picture: a screenshot of Windows Live Movie Maker. On the left is the preview window showing horses running on a beach under the title “Wild Horses”. On the right a purple box highlights the panel where the project’s video clips and title cards (“Wild”, “Directed by”, “Starring”) are laid out in order as a row of thumbnails.

What is the highlighted box below in Windows Movie Maker referring to?
questions.explain: Key: B. The highlighted area shows the clips arranged in order, which is the timeline (storyboard) where the video is assembled.

questions.stem: Which of the following stages of the creative process is associated with the user consulting with peers or supervisors regarding insights before pursuing the project further?
questions.explain: Key: D. Evaluation involves reviewing progress and getting feedback from peers or supervisors to judge whether to continue.

questions.stem: Software that can be used, modified, and sold to other users is BEST described as
questions.explain: Key: B. Open source software has freely available source code that users may use, modify and redistribute, including commercially.

questions.stem: The term ‘bandwidth’ refers to
options: the download speed of a connection
the number of IP addresses present in a network
the transmission capacity of a communication line
questions.explain: Key: D. Bandwidth is the maximum data transmission capacity of a communication channel.

questions.stem: Which of the following does NOT present an ethical issue in the field of Digital Media?
options: John sharing a video he shot and edited with his friends
John copying a commercial CD he borrowed from his friend
John selling a popular movie that he downloaded from YouTube
John downloading an expensive video suite from a file sharing site
questions.explain: Key: A. John owns the video he created, so sharing it raises no ethical issue; the others involve copyright infringement.

questions.stem:
This Item refers to the following picture.

Picture: two photographs side by side, joined by an arrow pointing from the left one to the right one. Each shows the black silhouette of a galloping horse against a yellow background above a dark strip of ground; the horse’s legs are in a different position in each frame, so together they form a short motion sequence (animation).

Which file format is BEST suited to this image? (The original item prints no question stem under the picture; this line is added by Kester Small.)
questions.explain: Key: B. GIF supports multiple frames, so it can store simple looping animations like the galloping horse; JPEG, EPS and TIFF are still-image formats.

questions.stem: Which of the following is achieved through the sensitive balance of variety and unity in colour?
questions.explain: Key: D. Colour harmony is the pleasing arrangement of colours that balances variety (interest) with unity (order).

questions.stem: A body of practical knowledge which provides guidance in colour mixing while noting the visual effects of colour combinations is called colour
questions.explain: Key: A. Colour theory is the body of guidance on mixing colours and on the visual effects of colour combinations.

questions.stem: Susan logged into a social networking site and posted a video of herself dancing. Soon, persons started sharing the video link across the internet. Which of the following ethical issues should be of concern to Susan?
questions.explain: Key: B. Her personal video is spreading beyond the audience she intended, which is a privacy concern.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST recent mode of live event streaming accepted by companies and individuals?
questions.explain: Key: B. A webcast broadcasts a live event over the internet; podcasts are pre-recorded and infographics are static graphics.

questions.stem: The mixture of a colour with black to reduce the lightness is called
questions.explain: Key: C. Adding black to a colour creates a shade; adding white creates a tint.

questions.stem: Which of the following activities could be considered a cybercrime?
options: Using a free software to develop an app
Opening customer data stored on a thumb drive
questions.explain: Key: B. Intercepting other people's communications without authorisation is illegal eavesdropping, a cybercrime.

questions.stem:
The item refers to the drawing canvas shown below.

Picture: a drawing program window. A toolbar of drawing tools (pen, eraser, fill, line, rectangle, ellipse, text, eyedropper and a stroke setting) runs down the left side; on the grid canvas is a coloured cartoon of a boy in a red helmet, orange shirt and blue jeans riding a green skateboard.

Max is contracted by Skaters International to create an animated logo for use in its social media marketing campaign. Which of the following describes scanned artwork which is further edited and finalized using artistic software?
questions.explain: Key: C. Artwork drawn by hand, scanned into a computer and then finished in software is digitized artwork.

questions.stem: Which of the following is MOST important in digital media and the internet?
questions.explain: Key: A. The internet's core value in digital media is enabling people to discover and access material (content) easily.

questions.stem: The act of acquiring digital content to be used in production is called
questions.explain: Key: A. Capturing is the process of acquiring digital content such as photos, video or audio for use in a production.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT needed to enhance entrepreneurship in the digital media industry?
questions.explain: Key: A. Continuous learning, a portfolio and marketing ability are key entrepreneurial assets; programming is a technical skill not essential to every digital media entrepreneur.

questions.stem:
This item refers to the following value chain

Diagram: five boxes joined by arrows, left to right: Content Creation → Aggregation & Publishing → Distribution (Fixed & Mobile) → Customer Environment → Stakeholder.

The stakeholder is MOST likely the
questions.explain: Key: A. The stakeholder sits at the end of the chain after the customer environment, so it represents the customer who consumes the content.

questions.stem:
Which of the following devices can be used to capture video?
I. Tablet PC
II. Smartphone
III. Graphics Tablet
questions.explain: Key: A. Tablet PCs and smartphones have built-in cameras; a graphics tablet is a pen input device with no camera.

questions.stem: Omar wants to seek funding for his business proposal. The banking sector does not want to take the risk of providing funding. What is the BEST alternative for his business proposal?
questions.explain: Key: D. Crowdfunding raises small amounts from many people online, avoiding traditional lenders who see the idea as too risky.

questions.stem: How does globalization impact the digital media expansion?
questions.explain: Key: C. Globalization opens worldwide markets and connections, speeding up the growth of digital media.

questions.stem:
Steven wants to start a music production business and requires a total of $100 000. [He has $50 000] in savings and his brother invests $25 000. He then acquires a $25 000 loan from the bank to make up for the total amount.
This type of funding can be BEST described as
questions.explain: Key: C. Savings and his brother's investment are equity, while the bank loan is debt, so the funding is a mix of both.

questions.stem: Which of the following may BEST enhance the employability of a digital media practitioner?
questions.explain: Key: D. A personal portfolio showcases a practitioner's skills and work to prospective employers and clients.

questions.stem: The creative process ends at the step known as
questions.explain: Key: D. Evaluation is the final stage, where the implemented solution is reviewed against the goals.

questions.stem: During which stage of the creative process is the individual required to take time to study the problem at hand and how the problem relates to its various components?
questions.explain: Key: A. Analysis involves studying the problem and how its parts relate before generating ideas.

questions.stem: Anila is designing an interactive map for her school’s website and wants to be able to highlight multiple locations on the map. Which of the following software would be BEST for implementing the map once it is created?
questions.explain: Key: D. Online mapping tools (such as Google My Maps) let users place multiple interactive markers and embed the map in a website.

questions.stem: Digital media tools have a significant and continuously changing impact on
questions.explain: Key: C. Digital media constantly reshapes the economy by creating new industries, business models and jobs.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a core preproduction task when facilitating digital video production?
questions.explain: Key: C. Lighting is set up and adjusted during production; logistics, budgeting and storyboarding are planned in preproduction.

questions.stem:
This item refers to the following diagram which shows an approach to the creative process.

Diagram: from Accept situation two arrows lead off. The upper arrow goes to Analysis, which splits to Ideate and to Define; both point to Select. The lower arrow goes to Define, which splits to Ideate (pointing to Select) and to Re-Analyze → Ideate (pointing up to Select). Select → Implement, which splits to Evaluate and to Re-Analyze; Re-Analyze also points to Evaluate.

Which of the following terms BEST describes this approach?
questions.explain: Key: C. The process splits into multiple alternative paths that later rejoin, which is a branched approach.

questions.stem: Kiara created a game to be played on mobile devices. It can be downloaded free of cost but upgrades for added features have to be purchased. This is known as a
questions.explain: Key: C. Freemium apps are free to download but charge for premium features or upgrades.

questions.stem: Marcus Banton is a graduate of a local high school in your country. He recently created an innovation for mobile phones. It is anticipated that sales in the mobile phone market will jump by over 43 per cent in the upcoming 18 months. Armed with this information, Marcus is concerned about selling his idea to manufacturers without getting any lifetime rewards for his invention. Which intellectual property will cover his invention and what lifetime reward he should seek?
options: Industrial Design, Rights to company shares
questions.explain: Key: B. Inventions are protected by patents, and licensing a patent earns the inventor ongoing royalties on each sale.

questions.stem: The first step in the creative process is
questions.explain: Key: C. The creative process begins with accepting the situation (acceptance) before analysis and definition.

questions.stem:
This item refers to the following picture.

Picture: a photograph of a Rottweiler leaping towards the camera over grass, with a concrete wall behind it. Two evenly spaced horizontal black lines and two evenly spaced vertical black lines are drawn over the photo, dividing it into nine equal rectangles; the dog’s head sits near the upper-left crossing point.

Which of the following terms accurately defines the overlay of black lines in the picture above?
questions.explain: Key: B. Two horizontal and two vertical lines dividing the frame into nine equal parts form the rule of thirds grid.

questions.stem: The MAIN rationale for the Creative Process in Digital Media is that
options: innovators are encouraged to provide new products, service including hardware and software that can create economic welfare and sustain small-business development
a wealth of resources are provided solely for online usage
the potentials of the human brain to think digitally is maximized
small business are created for the benefits of those living solely in small communities and Caribbean states
questions.explain: Key: A. The creative process drives innovation in products and services that generate economic welfare and sustain small businesses.

questions.stem:
This item refers to the following diagram

Diagram: a central square of four coloured blocks labelled media, technology, audience and impact, surrounded by six circles linked by arrows running clockwise in a cycle: product → optimize → markets → research → strategy → biz dev → back to product.

At what stage(s) of the production process would the diagram above be referred to?
options: Both in Preproduction and post production
questions.explain: Key: D. The cycle covers planning (research, strategy) and post-release activities (optimize, markets), so it is referred to in both preproduction and postproduction.

questions.stem: During an online match, a gamer in Grenada notices a delay between pressing a button and seeing the action on screen, even though his connection downloads large files quickly. This delay is BEST described as
questions.explain: Key: A. Latency is the time data take to travel from source to destination, felt as lag. Fast downloads show that his bandwidth (the amount of data per second) is good, so bandwidth is not the problem.

questions.stem: Which of the following characteristics distinguishes digital art from traditional artwork?
options: It exists as a single, unique tangible original
It can be edited, undone and refined without permanently altering the work
It is difficult to modify once a change has been made
It relies mainly on hand-crafted techniques with physical materials
questions.explain: Key: B. Digital art exists as digital files that are easy to edit (undo and refine). A unique tangible original, hand-crafted techniques and permanent changes all describe traditional artwork.

The marketing team of a villa in St Kitts needs to print its logo on a 3-metre billboard. Which file should the team use, and why?
options: File B, because SVG files use lossy compression to reduce file size
File A, because PNG files support transparency and therefore print more sharply
File B, because vector graphics are defined mathematically and scale without pixelation
File A, because its larger file size means it holds more detail
questions.explain: Key: C. Vector (SVG) artwork is stored as paths and shapes, so it can be enlarged to any size with no loss of quality. File A is only 800 × 800 pixels, so it would pixelate on a billboard; a larger file size does not mean it will scale, and SVG is not a lossy format.

questions.stem: Web 3.0 is MOST often described as the
options: read-write social web driven mainly by user-generated content
read-only web of static pages created by a small number of publishers
symbiotic web, in which humans and intelligent machines work together as partners
semantic and decentralised web, in which linked data allow machines to interpret meaning
questions.explain: Key: D. Web 3.0 is the semantic and decentralised web. Read-only describes Web 1.0, read-write/social describes Web 2.0 and the symbiotic web is Web 4.0.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are barriers that may prevent equal access to digital media in rural communities in Guyana?

I. Limited broadband infrastructure
II. The cost of devices and mobile data
III. Low levels of digital literacy
questions.explain: Key: D. Infrastructure, cost and education (including digital literacy) are all barriers to equal access, so all three statements apply.

questions.stem: The Barbados meteorological office publishes a web page with a colour-coded parish map and charts showing hourly rainfall levels. This product is BEST classified as
questions.explain: Key: D. Dashboards, maps, charts and data visualisations fall under data and information design. Immersive media, such as XR and virtual tours, places the user inside an environment, which a rainfall map does not do.

questions.stem: A Dominican animator produces a children's series narrated in Kwéyòl that features characters from local folklore. Which benefit of Caribbean-centric content does this BEST demonstrate?
options: It guarantees higher advertising revenue than imported content
It reduces production costs because local voices are always cheaper
It preserves culture and language while increasing global visibility for Caribbean creators
It removes the need for cultural sensitivity and audience awareness
questions.explain: Key: C. Using local language and folklore preserves heritage and showcases Caribbean creators to the world. Cost savings and guaranteed revenue are not assured, and Caribbean-centric content still requires cultural sensitivity.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST defines a digital media platform (DMP)?
options: A physical storage device used to archive digital media files
A set of laws that governs how content is distributed online
A digitised system for delivering video, audio and/or data to multiple networks such as cable, satellite and the Internet
A software application used only to edit audio and video
questions.explain: Key: C. A DMP is defined as a digitised platform for delivering video, audio and/or data to multiple networks (Telco, cable, satellite, digital terrestrial broadcasting, the Internet). Storage devices, editing software and laws are not delivery platforms.

questions.stem:
Item 9 refers to the following comparison of four platforms.
