The careers department of Sea-Almond Secondary School wants to publish detailed 20-minute video tutorials on CV writing that students can search for and return to later. Which platform is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Key: D. Platform Q supports long-form video that is searchable and organised into chapters, which suits 20-minute tutorials students revisit. Platform P limits clips to 60 seconds, and Platform S carries audio only.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are responsibilities of a good digital citizen?

I. Verifying sources before sharing information
II. Protecting the privacy of other people online
III. Sharing breaking news as widely and quickly as possible
questions.explain: Key: A. Verification of sources and privacy protection are listed responsibilities. Sharing news as quickly as possible, without checking it, spreads misinformation, so III is not a responsibility.

questions.stem: A Trinidadian company keeps the exact blend of spices in its pepper sauce known only to three staff members, who sign confidentiality agreements. The recipe is protected as a
questions.explain: Key: A. A trade secret is a confidential formula or process kept secret to give a business an advantage. A patent would require the recipe to be publicly disclosed; trademarks protect brand names and logos; industrial designs protect a product's appearance.

questions.stem: A Bahamian magazine pays a single fee for a stock photograph and may then use it in several issues without paying again. The photograph was MOST likely licensed as
questions.explain: Key: B. Royalty-free content is paid for once and can be reused within the licence terms. Rights-managed content is priced for each specific use, while public-domain and Creative Commons works are available without a fee.

questions.stem: A student asks an AI chatbot about the history of Fort Shirley in Dominica. It confidently gives a date and a quotation that cannot be found in any historical record. This risk of AI is known as
questions.explain: Key: D. AI hallucination occurs when a tool generates false information and presents it as fact. A deepfake is synthetic audio or video imitating a real person; bias is unfair skew in outputs; neither describes invented facts.

questions.stem: Which Creative Commons licence condition requires anyone who adapts a work to release the new version under the same licence terms?
questions.explain: Key: A. ShareAlike requires adaptations to carry the same licence. Attribution requires credit, NonCommercial forbids commercial use and NoDerivatives forbids adaptations altogether.

questions.stem: Before a new mobile payment app was publicly launched in Barbados, a small group of technology enthusiasts tested an early version, accepting its bugs and risks. In the technology adoption lifecycle, these users are
questions.explain: Key: D. Innovators are the first, most venturesome group, willing to try a product before it is proven. Early adopters follow once the product is launched and are opinion leaders; the early majority wait for evidence that it works.

questions.stem: Which of the following practices is MOST typical of a digital native?
options: Phoning a help desk rather than searching online for a solution
Learning a new skill by searching for short online video tutorials
Reading a device's printed manual fully before using it
questions.explain: Key: C. Digital natives grew up with digital technology and tend to learn by searching online and watching videos. Printing emails, phoning a help desk and reading printed manuals first are practices associated with digital immigrants.

questions.stem: In the digital media ecosystem, a body that sets and enforces rules for telecommunications providers across several Eastern Caribbean states is BEST classified as a(n)
questions.explain: Key: B. Regulators make and enforce rules for the industry. Infrastructure providers build and run the networks themselves, and distributors deliver content; neither sets the rules.

questions.stem: A Jamaican reggae artist now uploads her songs straight to streaming services instead of signing with a record label and a physical distributor. This change in the value chain is known as
questions.explain: Key: B. Disintermediation is the removal of intermediaries (here the label and physical distributor) so producers reach end-users directly. Aggregation is gathering content from many sources; convergence is the merging of technologies.

questions.stem: Marisol in Guyana earns income by completing hundreds of small online tasks, such as tagging images and transcribing ten-second audio clips, each paying a few cents. This work model is known as
questions.explain: Key: B. Micro-work involves very small, quickly completed online tasks paid individually. Telecommuting is doing a regular job from a remote location; hybrid work splits time between office and home.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are characteristics of the modern digital media work environment?

I. Project-based production for clients in different countries
II. Continuous learning to keep up with technological change
III. Guaranteed long-term employment with a single employer
questions.explain: Key: A. Project-based production, globalisation and continuous learning are characteristics of the modern digital media work environment. Freelancing, gig work and portfolio careers mean long-term employment with one employer is not guaranteed.

questions.stem: A Belizean app developer finds that several international platforms will not pay her earnings into a bank account in her country. This is an example of which regional challenge?
questions.explain: Key: B. Payment access is a recognised regional issue: creators may be unable to receive platform payouts. Market size, training and production infrastructure are separate challenges not described here.

questions.stem: Which section of a project proposal gives a brief overview of the whole project so that a busy funder can quickly understand its purpose, cost and expected benefits?
questions.explain: Key: D. The executive summary condenses the whole proposal into a short overview at the start. The introduction and background give context in more depth, the plan of action sets out tasks, and appendices hold supporting documents.

questions.stem:
Items 23–24 refer to the following timeline for Taste of Grenada, a student web series planned with the agile model.

WeekActivity
1Define goals, scope, tasks and a budget of EC$6 000
2–3Film and edit Episode 1 while tracking expenses
4Show Episode 1 to a focus group of 12 students; compare actual spending with the budget
5Re-edit Episode 1 using the feedback; adjust resources and schedule
6Release Episode 1 online; review overall performance and total costs
In the agile model, the activity in Week 4 represents the
questions.explain: Key: B. Review means evaluating completed work, gathering feedback and comparing actual spending with the planned budget, which is exactly what happens in Week 4. The sprint is Weeks 2–3 and iteration is Week 5.

questions.stem:
Items 23–24 refer to the following timeline for Taste of Grenada, a student web series planned with the agile model.

WeekActivity
1Define goals, scope, tasks and a budget of EC$6 000
2–3Film and edit Episode 1 while tracking expenses
4Show Episode 1 to a focus group of 12 students; compare actual spending with the budget
5Re-edit Episode 1 using the feedback; adjust resources and schedule
6Release Episode 1 online; review overall performance and total costs
In Week 4, the team finds it spent 30 per cent more than planned on equipment rental. According to the agile model, when should the budget be updated?
options: During the iteration stage in Week 5
Never, because the budget is fixed once the project starts
Only at the planning stage in Week 1
During the delivery stage in Week 6
questions.explain: Key: A. Iteration means making improvements, adjusting resources and timelines and updating the budget as needed, which is Week 5. Agile is flexible, so the budget is not fixed in Week 1, and waiting until delivery would be too late to act.

questions.stem: In a pitch for a Barbadian cooking app, the founder explains that the app will be downloaded from the major mobile app stores. Which of the 4Ps of marketing is she addressing?
questions.explain: Key: D. Place is where and how customers obtain the product, which here is the app stores. Promotion would describe how the app is advertised, and product would describe its features.

questions.stem: An angel investor gives a St Lucian animation studio US$40 000 in return for a 20 per cent share of the business. This is an example of
questions.explain: Key: D. Equity financing exchanges ownership (shares) for capital. Debt financing must be repaid with interest, and a grant does not take ownership.

questions.stem: A Trinidadian technology reviewer earns a commission each time a viewer buys a product through a special link in her video description. This creator income model is
questions.explain: Key: C. Affiliate marketing pays a commission for each sale made through the creator's tracked link. A brand partnership is a paid agreement with a brand, often a fixed fee, rather than payment per sale.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a DISPOSITION rather than a skill needed in the digital media industry?
questions.explain: Key: B. Dispositions are attitudes and habits of mind, such as openness to feedback, curiosity and resilience. Project management, pitching and financial literacy are skills that can be taught and practised.

questions.stem:
A group of CAPE students in St Kitts launches a crowdfunding campaign to pay for a documentary. Which of the following are advantages of this source of funding?

I. It can test public interest in the project before production
II. It requires the students to offer property as collateral
III. It can build a community of supporters before release
questions.explain: Key: B. Crowdfunding shows whether people care enough to pay and builds an audience early. Collateral is a requirement of bank loans (debt financing), not crowdfunding, so II is false.

questions.stem: A messaging app becomes more valuable to each user as more of that user's friends and family join it. This is known as
questions.explain: Key: C. A network effect occurs when a platform gains value as more people use it, a key feature of platform economies. The long tail refers to selling many niche items in small quantities.

questions.stem: In the creative design process, which stage comes immediately AFTER Definition?
questions.explain: Key: B. The sequence is Acceptance, Analysis, Definition, Ideation, Selection, Implementation, Evaluation. Once the problem is defined, ideas are generated (Ideation); Analysis comes before Definition.

questions.stem:
Item 32 refers to the following description of a diagram.

Acceptance → Analysis → Definition → Ideation → Selection → Implementation → Evaluation, with a single arrow leading from Evaluation back to Acceptance so that the whole sequence begins again.

Which method of implementing the creative process does the diagram illustrate?
questions.explain: Key: D. A cyclic model loops from the final stage back to the start so the process repeats. A linear model has no return arrow; stepped models have feedback loops between stages, and branched networks split into parallel paths.

questions.stem: To generate names for a new Bajan juice brand, a team writes the word “sunshine” on the board and each member quickly calls out the first related word that comes to mind. Which ideation technique are they using?
questions.explain: Key: D. Word association builds ideas by responding quickly to a prompt word. Mind mapping arranges ideas in branches around a central idea, and free writing is writing continuously without stopping.

questions.stem: A team designing a health app for elderly residents of Nevis interviews seniors, observes them using phones and tests large-button prototypes with them. This approach is BEST described as
questions.explain: Key: A. User-centred design involves the intended users throughout, through interviews, observation and testing. Designing for future needs focuses on anticipating later changes in technology or demand.

questions.stem: Before filming interviews with vendors in a Kingston market for a documentary, the producer asks each vendor to sign a form allowing the use of his or her image and voice. This document is a
questions.explain: Key: A. A talent (personal) release gives permission to record and use a person's likeness and voice. A location permit gives permission to film at a place, not to use a person's image.

questions.explain: Key: D. A close-up isolates a detail, here the wasted drop, to emphasise the message. Establishing the setting is the job of the wide shot in Frame 1.

questions.stem: When applying the rule of thirds to a portrait of a Carnival masquerader, the photographer should place the subject's eyes
options: along the upper horizontal line, near an intersection point
on the vertical centre line, with equal space on both sides
along the bottom edge of the frame
exactly in the centre of the frame
questions.explain: Key: A. The rule of thirds divides the frame into nine sections and places key features on the lines or their intersections; the eyes usually sit on the upper third line. Centring the subject is the approach the rule moves away from.

questions.stem: In a three-point lighting set-up for an interview, which light is used to soften the shadows created by the main light?
questions.explain: Key: B. The fill light, placed opposite the key light, softens its shadows. The key light is the main light that creates them, and the back light separates the subject from the background.

questions.stem: A Grenadian spa wants its website to communicate calm, relaxation and trust. Which colour palette is MOST appropriate?
questions.explain: Key: C. In colour psychology, blues suggest calm and trust and greens suggest nature and balance. Reds and oranges suggest energy and urgency, and black with neon yellow suggests warning.

questions.stem: A school club with no software budget needs to remove background hiss from a podcast recording. Which tool is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Key: B. Audacity is free, open-source audio software with noise-reduction tools. Adobe Audition can also do this but requires a paid subscription; GIMP edits images and Figma is for interface design.

questions.stem:
A student has finished a promotional video for her school and wants it to play on smartphones, laptops and smart TVs. Which of the following actions would improve device compatibility?

I. Exporting it as an MP4 file
II. Sharing only the editing software's project file
III. Testing playback on several devices before publishing
questions.explain: Key: B. MP4 plays on almost every device, and testing on several devices confirms compatibility. A project file opens only in the editing software, so II would prevent playback.

questions.stem: A CAPE class in Guyana wants every student to add, edit and update shared notes on one web page that keeps a history of all changes. Which communication tool is BEST?
questions.explain: Key: A. A wiki allows many users to edit the same pages collaboratively and keeps a revision history. A blog is usually written by one author in dated posts, with readers limited to commenting.

questions.stem: A designer needs a full-colour logo with a soft drop shadow and a transparent background for a website, with no loss of quality. Which file format is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Key: D. PNG is lossless, supports millions of colours and full (alpha) transparency, so soft shadows stay smooth. JPEG has no transparency, and GIF is limited to 256 colours with hard-edged transparency.

questions.stem:
Item 44 refers to the following file properties.

File namemashramani_recap.mov
Duration3 min 20 s
Resolution3840 × 2160 pixels
Frame rate60 fps
File size6.8 GB
The student must upload this file to the school's learning platform, which accepts files of up to 500 MB. Which change would reduce the file size MOST while keeping the video watchable on laptops?
options: Exporting it as an MP4 at 1920 × 1080 pixels and 30 fps
Exporting it as an uncompressed AVI file
Increasing the frame rate to 120 fps
Renaming the file extension from .mov to .mp4
questions.explain: Key: A. Re-exporting with compression at a lower resolution and frame rate cuts the data per second dramatically, and 1080p remains clear on laptops. Renaming the extension does not re-encode the video, and higher frame rates or uncompressed files make it bigger.

questions.stem: Which of the following would BEST show the design process in a student's digital proposal portfolio?
options: A list of the software the student has installed
Brainstorming notes, storyboards and drafts showing how the idea developed into the final product
Only the polished final product, exported at the highest resolution
Copies of professional work that inspired the student
questions.explain: Key: B. The portfolio is expected to show the design process from research to final solution, so evidence of brainstorming, planning and drafts is needed. A final product alone does not show the process.

questions.stem: Software or hardware that encodes and decodes digital audio or video, such as H.264, is called a
questions.explain: Key: B. A codec (coder–decoder) compresses and decompresses media data. A container, such as MP4 or MOV, is the file that holds the encoded streams but is not itself the encoder.

questions.stem:
Item 2 refers to the following properties of a photograph taken by Rhea at her home and posted on a public social media account.

Which item of information shown in the exhibit poses the GREATEST privacy risk now that the photograph is public?
questions.explain: Key: B. This metadata includes GPS coordinates that pinpoint where the photo was taken, here Rhea's home. The date is less sensitive on its own, and the camera model and dimensions reveal nothing about her location.

questions.stem: A video editor in Jamaica must reformat a 16:9 video so that it fills the screen on vertical short-form video platforms. Which aspect ratio should she use?
questions.explain: Key: A. Vertical full-screen video uses 9:16, the 16:9 landscape ratio turned on its side. 1:1 is square, 4:3 is an older TV shape and 21:9 is a cinematic widescreen ratio.

questions.stem: Web 5.0 is often called the “emotional web” because
options: content is limited to static pages with emotive images
web pages are written only to express the author's feelings
users mainly share emotional posts on social media
systems are expected to sense and respond to users' emotions
questions.explain: Key: D. Web 5.0 is the emotional or unseen web, where technology detects and reacts to human emotion. Sharing emotional posts is a feature of the social Web 2.0, and static pages describe Web 1.0.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST illustrates the transition from analogue to digital media?
options: A cinema adding more seats to its main screen
A radio station replacing its reel-to-reel tapes with audio files stored on a server
A newspaper increasing the number of copies it prints each day
A photographer switching from colour film to black-and-white film
questions.explain: Key: B. Moving from tape (analogue) to files stored as binary data (digital) is the analogue-to-digital transition. Switching film types keeps the photographer within analogue media.

questions.stem: A Guyanese bank commissions a 60-second video in which moving text, icons and simple animated characters explain how to use its mobile app. This product is BEST described as a(n)
questions.explain: Key: B. Explainer videos using motion graphics and animated characters fall under animation and motion graphics. An infographic presents information visually but is static, and a podcast is audio only.

questions.stem:
A designer in Curaçao is choosing a platform on which to sell her digital art prints. Which of the following should she consider?

I. The platform's terms of service
II. Whether the platform can pay sellers based in the Caribbean
III. The file specifications required for uploads
questions.explain: Key: D. Terms of service, Caribbean market access and file specifications are all platform considerations, so all three apply.

questions.stem:
Item 8 refers to the following feature comparison of four digital media platforms.

FeaturePlatform 1Platform 2Platform 3Platform 4
Product catalogue and shopping cartYesNoNoNo
Online paymentsYesNoNoYes (donations only)
Course modules, quizzes and grade bookNoYesNoNo
Live video and replaysNoNoYesYes
Based on its features, Platform 2 is MOST likely a(n)
questions.explain: Key: A. Course modules, quizzes and a grade book are the defining features of an e-learning platform. Platform 1, with a catalogue, cart and payments, is the e-commerce platform.

questions.stem: Three years after posting offensive comments online at age 15, Andre is turned down for an internship when the company finds the posts. This illustrates the pitfall of
questions.explain: Key: C. Online posts form a lasting record (digital footprint) that others can find years later. Andre's comments may have been offensive, but the pitfall shown is the lasting record that damaged his opportunities.

questions.stem: A social media page deliberately posts a fake government notice claiming that all schools in Trinidad will close for a month, intending to cause panic. This is BEST described as
questions.explain: Key: A. Disinformation is false information spread deliberately to mislead. Misinformation is false information shared without intent to deceive, for example by someone who believes the notice is real.

questions.stem: A Jamaican company registers the distinctive shape of its new rum bottle so that competitors cannot copy its appearance. This shape is protected as a(n)
questions.explain: Key: A. Industrial designs protect the unique appearance of a product, such as its shape or packaging. Patents protect how an invention works, not how it looks, and a trade secret must stay confidential, which a bottle on shelves cannot.

questions.stem: An e-book bought from an online store cannot be copied to another person's device or printed. Which technology is MOST likely responsible for these limits?
questions.explain: Key: B. Digital rights management (DRM) is technology that controls how digital content is accessed, copied and shared, for example in e-books. Creative Commons and open access are designed to make sharing easier, not to block it.

questions.stem: A Barbadian news website uses AI to generate illustrations for its articles. Which practice BEST shows ethical use of AI?
options: Generating realistic images of real people without their consent
Presenting the images as photographs taken by staff
Removing all human review to publish faster
Clearly labelling the images as AI-generated
questions.explain: Key: D. Transparency and acknowledgement of AI-assisted work are key ethical principles. Passing images off as photographs, using real people's likeness without consent and removing human oversight all breach them.

questions.stem: A St Lucian online store sells handmade soap to customers living in the European Union. Which framework sets out rules it must follow when collecting those customers' personal data?
questions.explain: Key: D. The GDPR applies to organisations anywhere that process the personal data of people in the EU. The UDHR sets out broad human rights and WIPO deals with intellectual property; neither gives detailed data-protection rules.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes open-source software from a work in the public domain?
options: A public-domain work must always be credited, while open-source software need not be
Open-source software can never be sold, while a public-domain work can be sold
Both are owned by governments and are free only to citizens
Open-source software is released under a licence with conditions, while a public-domain work has no copyright restrictions
questions.explain: Key: D. Open-source software stays under copyright and is shared through a licence (for example the GPL) with terms to follow. Public-domain works are free of copyright entirely. Open-source software can be sold, and the public domain does not legally require credit.

questions.stem: Mr. Henry, aged 62, learned to make video calls during the pandemic. He prints important emails and would rather phone a colleague than send a text message. Mr. Henry is BEST described as a
questions.explain: Key: C. A digital immigrant adopted digital technology later in life and often keeps habits from before it, such as printing emails. A digital nomad is someone who works remotely while travelling.

questions.stem: A Jamaican teenager watches dancehall videos online and also records and uploads her own dance tutorials. She is BEST described as a
questions.explain: Key: C. A prosumer both consumes and produces content. Calling her only a consumer ignores the tutorials she creates.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are elements of the digital media ecosystem?

I. Advertisers
II. Payment systems
III. Typewriter manufacturers
questions.explain: Key: A. Advertisers and payment systems are elements of the digital media ecosystem. Typewriter manufacturers produce analogue equipment and play no part in creating, distributing or paying for digital media.

questions.stem:
Item 19 refers to the following value chain for a soca album released by a Trinidadian artist.

StageActivity
1The artist writes and records the songs
2A producer mixes and masters the tracks
3A digital distributor (aggregator) delivers the album to many streaming services
4Streaming platforms make the album available to subscribers
5Listeners stream the album on their phones
In Stage 3, the digital distributor MAINLY
options: creates the original songs and lyrics
provides the internet connection that listeners use
chooses the order of songs on each listener's playlist
collects music from many artists and supplies it to multiple streaming platforms
questions.explain: Key: D. An aggregator gathers content from many creators and delivers it to many platforms, linking production to distribution. Writing songs is Stage 1, and internet access comes from infrastructure providers.

questions.stem: When a major undersea cable linking several Eastern Caribbean islands is damaged, creators, platforms, advertisers and audiences are all affected. This BEST illustrates
options: interdependence among players in the digital media ecosystem
questions.explain: Key: C. Every player relies on the shared infrastructure, so a failure in one part spreads to the others. Disintermediation is the removal of intermediaries, which does not happen here.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST shows the effect of globalisation on the digital media work environment?
options: A local radio station hiring only staff who live in the same town
A school limiting the use of mobile phones in class
A Vincentian illustrator working from home for clients in Canada, Japan and the United Kingdom
A printing press adding new local delivery routes
questions.explain: Key: C. Globalisation links markets worldwide, allowing a Caribbean creator to serve clients in many countries. The other options describe local activity only.

questions.stem: A Barbadian advertising agency contracts a company in another country to handle all the subtitling of its videos. This is an example of
questions.explain: Key: A. Outsourcing means contracting an outside company to carry out a business function. Micro-work refers to individuals doing tiny paid tasks, not a company taking over a whole function.

questions.stem: The high cost of mobile data in some Caribbean territories limits how much video audiences can stream. In an analysis of the environment, this is BEST classified as a(n)
questions.explain: Key: C. Cost and affordability are economic factors. Political factors concern government policy, social factors concern demographics and lifestyle, and cultural factors concern beliefs, language and traditions.

questions.stem: In a proposal for a youth mental-health podcast in Dominica, which section would contain the statement “Many teenagers in rural communities have no confidential place to learn about mental health”?
questions.explain: Key: B. The problem statement describes the need the project will address. Objectives set out what the project will achieve, and evaluation explains how success will be measured.

questions.stem:
Item 25 refers to the following timeline for a short documentary about a Jamaican fishing village.

TaskPlanned weeks
Research and scriptwritingWeeks 1–2
Location scoutingWeek 2
FilmingWeeks 3–4
Editing (starts only after filming ends)Weeks 5–6
Publishing (starts only after editing ends)Week 7
Filming starts one week later than planned because of a tropical storm. If every task keeps its planned length, in which week will publishing now take place?
questions.explain: Key: B. Filming moves to Weeks 4–5, editing (two weeks, after filming) moves to Weeks 6–7, and publishing therefore moves from Week 7 to Week 8. The one-week delay carries through every dependent task.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST describes the agile approach to project management?
options: All requirements are fixed at the start and cannot be changed
The client is consulted only when the final product is delivered
Each phase must be fully completed before the next begins, with no revisiting
Work is delivered in small increments, with frequent feedback and adaptation to change
questions.explain: Key: D. Agile is iterative and incremental, emphasising flexibility, collaboration and continuous delivery. Fixed requirements and strictly sequential phases describe a traditional linear (waterfall) approach.

questions.stem: In a pitch to a regional creative-industries fund, which part of the pitch states, “We are seeking US$25 000 to cover equipment and the first six months of production”?
questions.explain: Key: C. The ask states exactly what the presenter wants from the audience, usually an amount of money and its use. Traction shows progress already achieved.

questions.stem: Which source of funding normally does NOT have to be repaid AND does NOT require giving away a share of ownership?
options: A loan from a commercial bank
A grant from a cultural agency
questions.explain: Key: D. Grants are awarded to approved projects and do not need to be repaid. Bank loans must be repaid with interest, while venture capitalists and angel investors take equity in return.

questions.stem:
Which of the following would be classified as debt financing for a digital media start-up?

I. A crowdfunding campaign in which backers receive a T-shirt
II. A bank loan repaid with interest over three years
III. A loan from a credit union to buy cameras
questions.explain: Key: C. Debt financing is borrowed money that must be repaid, as with bank and credit-union loans. Reward-based crowdfunding is not repaid; backers receive a reward instead.

questions.stem: After her first three online videos get very few views, Shania in Antigua studies her analytics, redesigns her thumbnails and keeps posting every week. Which disposition is she MAINLY showing?
questions.explain: Key: C. Resilience is the ability to recover from setbacks and keep going. Professionalism concerns conduct and reliability in work with others, which is not the focus here.

questions.stem: At which stage of the creative design process does a designer recognise the problem and commit to solving it?
questions.explain: Key: B. Acceptance is the first stage, where the designer accepts the challenge. Analysis follows, gathering information about the problem.

questions.stem: After producing twelve possible logo concepts for a Grenadian chocolate company, a design team scores each one against the client's brief and keeps the strongest two. Which stage of the creative design process are they in?
questions.explain: Key: B. Selection is choosing the best ideas from those generated. Ideation produced the twelve concepts, and evaluation judges the final solution after it has been implemented.

questions.stem:
Item 33 refers to the following description of a diagram.

Acceptance → Analysis → Definition → Ideation → Selection → Implementation → Evaluation. After each stage there is a checkpoint; if the checkpoint is not passed, an arrow leads back to the stage just completed before the team may continue.

The approach shown in the diagram is BEST described as
questions.explain: Key: C. Checkpoints that send the team back to the stage just completed are intermediate feedback loops. A cyclic model has one loop from the end back to the start, and a linear model has no loops at all.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are advantages of using open-source tools such as GIMP and Audacity in a school media lab?

I. There is no licence fee
II. The software can be improved by a community of developers
III. Official telephone support is guaranteed by the publisher
questions.explain: Key: A. Open-source tools are free to use and are developed by communities. They usually rely on forums and documentation for help rather than guaranteed official support, so III is false.

questions.stem: A team building a tourism app for Belize designs it so that new languages and augmented-reality features can be added later as technology improves. This BEST reflects
questions.explain: Key: A. Designing for future needs anticipates later changes in technology and demand. User-centred design focuses on involving today's users in shaping the product.

questions.stem: What is the MAIN purpose of pre-production?
options: To promote the finished product to audiences
To plan the content, audience, format, message and resources before production begins
To edit and colour-grade the recorded footage
To export the final product in suitable formats
questions.explain: Key: B. Pre-production is the planning phase before any recording. Editing and colour grading belong to post-production, as does exporting.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are core elements to address in pre-production for a music video to be filmed on a public beach in Jamaica?

I. Obtaining a location permit
II. Colour grading the footage
III. Planning for the health and safety of cast and crew
questions.explain: Key: B. Permits and health and safety are core pre-production elements. Colour grading is done in post-production, after filming.

questions.stem:
Items 38–39 refer to the following storyboard for a 45-second promotional video for an eco-lodge in Guyana.

PanelShotAudioDuration
1Aerial wide shot over the rainforest canopy at sunriseBirdsong; music fades in8 s
2Medium shot of a guide pointing to a giant river otterGuide's voice-over10 s
3Close-up of a guest's smiling faceMusic7 s
4Low-angle shot of the lodge at dusk; text “Book your stay”Music10 s
5Logo and website addressMusic ends5 s
The producer notices that the storyboard does not match the 45-second brief. Which change would make the running time exactly 45 seconds?
questions.explain: Key: B. The panels total 8 + 10 + 7 + 10 + 5 = 40 seconds, so 5 seconds must be added. Extending Panel 3 by 5 seconds gives 45; shortening Panel 1 or removing Panel 5 gives 35, and extending Panel 2 by 2 seconds gives only 42.

questions.stem:
Items 38–39 refer to the following storyboard for a 45-second promotional video for an eco-lodge in Guyana.

PanelShotAudioDuration
1Aerial wide shot over the rainforest canopy at sunriseBirdsong; music fades in8 s
2Medium shot of a guide pointing to a giant river otterGuide's voice-over10 s
3Close-up of a guest's smiling faceMusic7 s
4Low-angle shot of the lodge at dusk; text “Book your stay”Music10 s
5Logo and website addressMusic ends5 s
The low-angle shot of the lodge in Panel 4 is MOST likely intended to
options: show a guest's point of view from a window of the lodge
hide the surrounding rainforest from view
make the lodge appear impressive and grand
make the lodge appear small and vulnerable
questions.explain: Key: C. A low-angle shot looks up at the subject, making it seem larger and more powerful. A high-angle shot looking down makes a subject seem small and vulnerable.

questions.stem: A photographer in St Lucia positions the camera so that a winding road draws the viewer's eye towards the Pitons in the distance. Which compositional technique is she using?
questions.explain: Key: B. Leading lines are lines in a scene, such as roads or rivers, that guide the eye towards the subject. The rule of thirds concerns where the subject is placed within a grid, not how the eye is guided to it.

questions.stem: Volunteers for a Trinidadian charity live on different islands and need to design social media graphics together in real time, using only web browsers on low-cost laptops. Which tool is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Key: C. Canva runs in a browser, has a free tier and supports real-time collaboration on graphics. Photoshop must be installed, needs a paid licence and demands more powerful hardware; Audacity edits audio and DaVinci Resolve edits video.

questions.stem: Which is a disadvantage of relying on a cloud-based video editor for a school project in an area with unreliable internet service?
options: Projects can be exported only as GIF files
Files cannot be shared with other team members
The tool can be used on only one device
Work may be interrupted or lost when the connection drops
questions.explain: Key: D. Cloud tools depend on a stable connection, so outages interrupt work. Easy sharing and access from several devices are in fact advantages of cloud tools.

questions.stem: A church in Montserrat wants members living overseas to watch its Easter service as it happens and post comments in real time. Which communication method is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Key: B. Live streaming broadcasts video in real time with live chat. A podcast is recorded audio listened to later, so members could not take part as the service happens.

questions.stem:
Item 44 refers to the following properties of an interview recording.

File nameinterview_raw.wav
FormatWAV (uncompressed PCM)
Sample rate / bit depth48 kHz / 24-bit
ChannelsStereo
Duration45 min
File size777 MB
The student wants to publish this interview as a podcast episode that listeners can download quickly on mobile data. Which export setting is MOST appropriate?
options: MP4 video with a still image at 4K resolution
questions.explain: Key: A. MP3 uses lossy compression; at 128 kbps a 45-minute episode is about 43 MB instead of 777 MB, and quality is fine for speech. Higher-resolution WAV and AIFF files are uncompressed and even larger.

questions.stem: When preparing slides for a digital proposal presentation to be shown in a large classroom, which practice BEST supports clear visual communication?
options: Using many different fonts to keep viewers interested
Filling each slide with full paragraphs so nothing is missed
Placing all text over a busy photographic background
Using high-contrast text and a few key points on each slide
questions.explain: Key: D. High contrast and brief key points are readable from a distance. Dense text, busy backgrounds and mixed fonts reduce legibility and distract the audience.

questions.stem: An online guide to Fort George in Grenada lets visitors click on images, audio clips and video to jump to related content. This is BEST described as
questions.explain: Key: A. Hypermedia links multiple media types (images, audio, video and text). Hypertext links text only, so it does not cover the audio and video links here.

questions.stem: Which statement about lossy compression is correct?
options: It increases image resolution to improve quality
It is used only for vector graphics
It permanently removes some data to reduce file size, as in JPEG and MP3 files
It reduces file size without losing any data, as in PNG and ZIP files
questions.explain: Key: C. Lossy compression discards data the viewer or listener is unlikely to notice, and the loss cannot be undone. Reducing size without losing data describes lossless compression.

questions.stem:
Item 3 refers to the following file properties.

File namebeach_banner.jpg
Dimensions1200 × 400 pixels
Resolution72 ppi
Colour profilesRGB
The image is to be printed at a quality of 300 ppi. What is the largest print width that maintains this quality?
questions.explain: Key: D. Print width = pixels ÷ ppi = 1200 ÷ 300 = 4 inches. 16.7 inches is the width at 72 ppi, which would look blurred in print.

questions.stem: A Barbadian journalist uses one smartphone to record video, edit it, write the story and publish it online. This BEST illustrates
questions.explain: Key: A. Convergence is the merging of several media functions and technologies into one device or platform. Multicasting is sending one stream to many receivers at once.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST illustrates the disruption of an industry by digital media?
options: A cinema adding a weekly screening of local films
A radio station buying new studio microphones
A newspaper adding a website alongside its print edition
Video rental stores closing as customers switch to streaming services
questions.explain: Key: D. Disruption occurs when a business model declines because it fails to adapt to digital alternatives. A newspaper adding a website is an example of adapting to digital media, not being disrupted by it.

questions.stem: A hotel in St Kitts hires someone to research keywords and improve how high its website appears in search engine results. This job role is
questions.explain: Key: C. Search Engine Optimisation (SEO) analysts improve a site's ranking in search results. UX/UI designers focus on how users experience and interact with the interface.

questions.stem: A music streaming service suggests calypso playlists to a listener in Trinidad based on the songs she has played before. This is an example of
questions.explain: Key: C. Algorithms that analyse a user's behaviour to tailor recommendations and feeds are described as personalisation. DRM controls access to content; it does not recommend it.

questions.stem: A museum app in The Bahamas lets visitors point their phone at a shipwreck exhibit and see a 3D model of the ship appear on screen over the real display. This is an example of
questions.explain: Key: A. Augmented reality overlays digital content on the real world seen through a device. Virtual reality replaces the real world with a fully computer-generated environment.

questions.stem:
A content creator is producing a travel series about Garifuna communities in St Vincent and Belize. Which of the following practices show ethical representation and cultural sensitivity?

I. Consulting community members about how they wish to be portrayed
II. Adding subtitles so that the series is accessible to more viewers
III. Exaggerating customs to make the series more dramatic
questions.explain: Key: A. Consultation and accessibility fall under ethical representation and audience awareness. Exaggerating customs misrepresents the community, so III is unethical.

questions.stem:
Item 10 refers to the following comparison of four community platforms considered by a youth NGO in Guyana.

PlatformMonthly costModeration toolsData privacy
AlphaFreeBasicShares user data with advertisers
BetaUS$10Advanced (filters, reporting, age controls)Does not sell data; meets GDPR standards
GammaFreeNoneDoes not sell data
DeltaUS$40Advanced (filters, reporting, age controls)Does not sell data; meets GDPR standards
The NGO works with children, must protect members' data, needs strong moderation tools and has a monthly budget of US$15. Which platform should it choose?
questions.explain: Key: D. Beta is the only platform that has advanced moderation, does not sell data and is within the US$15 budget. Delta meets the needs but costs US$40; Gamma has no moderation; Alpha shares data with advertisers.

questions.stem: Which of the following is protected by copyright rather than by a patent or a trademark?
options: A new hinge mechanism for folding phones
The name of a clothing brand
A new method for compressing video files
The recorded audio of a podcast episode
questions.explain: Key: D. Copyright protects original creative works such as recordings, films and writing. New methods and mechanisms are inventions protected by patents, and brand names are protected by trademarks.

questions.stem: In a critical review for class, a CAPE student quotes two lines of a published poem and credits the poet. This use is MOST likely permitted under
questions.explain: Key: A. Fair dealing (fair use) allows limited use of copyrighted material for purposes such as criticism, review and education, with acknowledgement. DRM is a technical control, not a legal permission.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are RISKS of using AI in digital media production?

I. Deepfakes that impersonate real people
II. Automatic captions that make video accessible
III. Over-reliance on AI tools, leading to loss of originality
questions.explain: Key: B. Key risks include deepfakes, over-reliance and loss of originality. Automatic captioning is a benefit because it improves accessibility.

questions.stem: A student in Belize receives an email that appears to come from her bank, asking her to “confirm” her password through a link. This is an example of
questions.explain: Key: B. Phishing is a cybercrime that uses fake messages to trick people into giving away personal details, which can lead to identity theft. Piracy is the illegal copying of content.

questions.stem: A Caribbean government publishes tourism arrival statistics online in a downloadable format that anyone may use and republish freely. This is an example of
questions.explain: Key: B. Open data is data made freely available for anyone to use and share. Open source applies to software source code, not statistics.

questions.stem: Which belief is MOST typical of digital natives?
options: New technology is best learned from formal manuals
Information should be instantly available and easy to share
Printed information is always more trustworthy than online information
Important communication should take place face to face or by telephone
questions.explain: Key: B. Digital natives expect instant, always-on access and sharing. Trust in print, reliance on manuals and a preference for phone calls are attitudes associated with digital immigrants.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an emerging trend in the digital media industry?
options: Decreasing use of analytics by marketers
A move away from mobile devices to desktop-only content
Growth of short-form vertical video and AI-assisted production
Replacement of streaming by sales of physical DVDs
questions.explain: Key: C. Short-form vertical video and AI-assisted production are among the fastest-growing trends at the time of writing (2026). Mobile use, analytics and streaming are all increasing, not declining.

questions.stem: A Grenadian news website uses software that lets journalists write, edit, schedule and publish articles without writing any code. In the digital media ecosystem, this software is a
questions.explain: Key: D. A content management system (CMS) manages the creation and publishing of web content. Infrastructure providers supply networks and hosting, not editing and publishing tools.

questions.stem:
Item 19 refers to the following value chain for Island Reads, a small Caribbean e-book publisher.

Author writes the manuscript → Editor and designer prepare the e-book file → E-book platform sets the price, applies DRM and sells the download → Reader buys and reads the book on a tablet

Compared with a traditional print value chain, which activity has been REMOVED from this value chain?
options: Printing, warehousing and shipping physical books
questions.explain: Key: B. Digital distribution delivers a file directly, so printing, storing and shipping books are no longer needed. Writing, editing and payment still take place in the digital chain.

questions.stem: On a Jamaican cooking channel hosted on a video-sharing platform, which stakeholder pays the platform to place messages before and during the videos?
questions.explain: Key: B. Advertisers pay platforms to reach audiences, and the platform shares some of that revenue with the creator. Viewers usually watch for free, and the creator receives revenue rather than paying it.

questions.stem: A design agency in Roseau requires staff to work in the office on Mondays and Thursdays and from home on the other weekdays. This work model is
questions.explain: Key: D. Hybrid work combines office-based and remote days. Gig work involves short-term contracts with no fixed employer.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are typical features of gig work in the digital media industry?

I. Short-term, task-based contracts
II. Payment per project rather than a fixed salary
III. Employer-provided pension and health benefits
questions.explain: Key: A. Gig workers take short contracts and are paid per job. They are usually independent contractors, so pensions and health benefits are not provided by an employer.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST example of a regional OPPORTUNITY in the digital media industry?
options: Using social media to market Caribbean festivals to the diaspora and international tourists
Small local audiences for niche content
Limited broadband access in rural areas
The high cost of importing production equipment
questions.explain: Key: A. Reaching wider markets, such as the diaspora and tourists, is listed as an opportunity. Equipment cost, limited broadband and small audiences are challenges.

questions.stem:
Items 24–25 refer to the following project record for a school timetable app in Belize, managed with the agile model.

DaysActivity
1Planning meeting: goals, feature list and a total budget of US$1 200
2–11Sprint 1: build the log-in and timetable features (planned spending US$400)
12Review: demonstration to 15 students; actual Sprint 1 spending was US$450
13–15?
16–25Sprint 2: build the homework-reminder feature
According to the agile model, what should MOST likely happen during Days 13–15?
options: The team begins writing the executive summary of its proposal
The team releases the finished app to all students and closes the project
The team repeats the planning meeting and discards the Sprint 1 work
The team improves the features using the student feedback and adjusts the budget and timeline
questions.explain: Key: D. After a review comes iteration: making improvements and adjusting resources, timelines and budget. Delivery happens only at the end, and agile builds on completed work rather than discarding it.

questions.stem:
Items 24–25 refer to the following project record for a school timetable app in Belize, managed with the agile model.

DaysActivity
1Planning meeting: goals, feature list and a total budget of US$1 200
2–11Sprint 1: build the log-in and timetable features (planned spending US$400)
12Review: demonstration to 15 students; actual Sprint 1 spending was US$450
13–15?
16–25Sprint 2: build the homework-reminder feature
By what percentage did Sprint 1 spending exceed its planned amount?
questions.explain: Key: D. The overspend is US$450 − US$400 = US$50, and 50 ÷ 400 × 100 = 12.5%. Dividing by the total budget (US$1 200) or by the actual spend (US$450) gives the wrong base.

questions.stem: Which section of a proposal explains how the team will measure whether the project met its objectives, for example by tracking downloads and survey results?
questions.explain: Key: A. The evaluation section explains how success will be measured. Benefits describe the expected positive outcomes but not how they will be checked.

questions.stem: In her pitch, a Trinidadian founder states that her app gained 8 000 users in three months and has signed a partnership with a local bank. This part of the pitch shows
questions.explain: Key: C. Traction is evidence of progress, such as users, revenue or partnerships. The ask states what the founder wants from investors.

questions.stem: A Barbadian comic artist collects payment from fans for her graphic novel two months before it is published, and uses the money to pay for printing. This type of funding is
questions.explain: Key: C. Pre-sales fund production by selling the product before it is completed. No loan or share of ownership is involved, so it is neither debt nor equity.

questions.stem: Which source of funding typically gives a start-up a small investment together with mentoring over a fixed programme of a few months, often ending with a demonstration day for investors?
questions.explain: Key: D. Accelerators run short, cohort-based programmes that combine investment, mentoring and a demo day. Banks and credit unions provide loans without mentoring programmes.

questions.stem: A video editor teaches herself a new AI-assisted editing tool soon after it is released. She is MAINLY showing
options: adaptability and a commitment to continuous learning
questions.explain: Key: D. Learning new tools as technology changes shows adaptability and continuous learning, which the digital media industry values highly. Risk appetite concerns willingness to take business or financial risks.

questions.stem: The creative design process is BEST defined as
options: the final stage of editing a video
a structured series of stages that moves from a problem to an evaluated solution
a set of software tools used by designers
a single burst of inspiration that produces a finished product
questions.explain: Key: B. The creative design process is a structured sequence, from Acceptance to Evaluation, that turns a problem into a tested solution. It is not a single moment of inspiration or a set of tools.

questions.stem: A team planning a campaign to reduce plastic waste on Grenada's beaches surveys residents and studies waste-collection data before writing a precise statement of the problem. Which stage of the creative design process are they in?
questions.explain: Key: D. Analysis involves researching the problem and gathering data. It comes before Definition, where the precise problem statement is written; ideation would mean generating solutions.

questions.stem: A Dominican environmental group wants to post regular articles with photos about its beach clean-ups, listed by date, on which readers can leave comments. Which communication method is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Key: A. A blog publishes dated posts, usually by one author or group, with reader comments. A wiki is for many users editing shared pages, which the group does not need.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MAIN disadvantage of a linear method of implementing the creative process?
options: It never reaches the evaluation stage
It offers little opportunity to return to earlier stages when problems are found
It has too many feedback loops to manage
It requires several teams working on parallel paths
questions.explain: Key: B. A linear model moves through the stages once in a fixed order, so it is hard to go back and fix problems. Multiple feedback loops and parallel paths describe stepped and branched models.

questions.stem: A large project team splits into groups that explore different solution paths at the same time; the paths later rejoin when the best solution is selected. Which method of implementing the creative process is this?
questions.explain: Key: B. A branched network divides the process into parallel paths that later rejoin. Stepped models have feedback loops but follow a single path.

questions.stem: In the Design Thinking model, which stage involves observing and interviewing users to understand their feelings and needs?
questions.explain: Key: C. Empathise is the first Design Thinking stage, focused on understanding users. Define comes next, turning those insights into a clear problem statement.

questions.stem: Before designing a brand identity for a coffee shop in Curaçao, a designer collects photographs, colour swatches, textures and font samples on one board to agree the look and feel with the client. This is a
questions.explain: Key: D. A mood board gathers visual references to set the style and feel of a project. A storyboard plans shots in sequence, and a wireframe plans the layout of a screen.

questions.stem: Which pre-production item shows the basic layout of a web page, including where the menu, images and text blocks will go, without the final colours or images?
questions.explain: Key: B. A wireframe is a simple layout plan for a page or screen. A mood board sets the look and feel but does not show layout.

questions.stem:
Items 39–40 refer to the following storyboard for a 20-second tree-planting announcement in Antigua.

ShotDescriptionAudioTime
1Wide shot from the road: a bare hillside scarred by erosion after heavy rainRain4 s
2Medium shot: students carrying seedlings up the hillUpbeat steelpan music6 s
3Close-up: hands pressing soil around a seedlingMusic4 s
4Wide shot from the same spot on the road, one year later: the hillside is green. Text: “Roots hold our island together.”Music ends6 s
Which purpose of a storyboard is BEST demonstrated by this document?
options: It records the final editing decisions made in post-production
It lists equipment costs for the budget
It gives legal permission to film on the hillside
It lets the team see the sequence of shots, audio and timing before filming
questions.explain: Key: D. A storyboard is a pre-production plan showing each shot, its audio and duration in order. It is not a budget, an edit record or a permit.

questions.stem:
Items 39–40 refer to the following storyboard for a 20-second tree-planting announcement in Antigua.

ShotDescriptionAudioTime
1Wide shot from the road: a bare hillside scarred by erosion after heavy rainRain4 s
2Medium shot: students carrying seedlings up the hillUpbeat steelpan music6 s
3Close-up: hands pressing soil around a seedlingMusic4 s
4Wide shot from the same spot on the road, one year later: the hillside is green. Text: “Roots hold our island together.”Music ends6 s
Shots 1 and 4 use the same location and framing MAINLY to
options: show a clear before-and-after contrast that supports the message
avoid the need for a location permit
establish the identity of the main character
reduce the number of camera operators needed
questions.explain: Key: A. Repeating the framing lets the audience compare the eroded and the green hillside directly, reinforcing the message. Matching the framing has no effect on permits or crew size.

questions.stem: A Jamaican public-health poster warns residents about dengue fever and must grab attention and signal danger. Which colour is MOST appropriate as the dominant accent?
questions.explain: Key: D. In colour psychology, red signals danger and urgency and attracts attention. Pale blue and pastel green suggest calm and safety, which would weaken a warning.

questions.stem:
Which of the following would improve the sound quality of an interview recorded outdoors on a beach in Belize?

I. Placing the recorder next to the speakers of a nearby beach bar
II. Clipping a lavalier microphone close to the speaker's mouth
III. Fitting a windscreen to the microphone
questions.explain: Key: C. A lavalier microphone near the mouth captures the voice clearly, and a windscreen reduces wind noise. Recording next to loudspeakers would add unwanted background music.

questions.stem: Which factor is MOST important when evaluating whether a digital media tool suits a project?
options: Whether it is the most expensive option available
Whether it was released within the last month
Whether it can produce the required output for the project's purpose and audience
questions.explain: Key: D. Tools should be evaluated for suitability based on purpose, audience, project needs, resources and expected output. Price, newness and popularity do not show that a tool fits the task.

questions.stem:
Item 44 refers to the following export settings chosen by a student.

ProjectSports Day highlights (with commentary and music)
Export formatGIF
Resolution1920 × 1080 pixels
Duration2 min 30 s
Estimated file size410 MB
The student wants to share the video on social media. What is the MAIN problem with these export settings?
options: 1920 × 1080 pixels is too low a resolution for social media
GIF files cannot be displayed on smartphones
GIF files carry no audio and become very large for long clips, so MP4 should be used
The video is too short to be accepted by social media platforms
questions.explain: Key: C. GIF is meant for short, silent loops. The commentary and music would be lost and the file would be huge, while an MP4 with compression keeps the sound at a fraction of the size. 1080p is a standard social media resolution.

questions.stem:
Which of the following formats can be exported from a digital media project for viewing on most digital devices?

I. MP4
II. PDF
III. GIF
questions.explain: Key: D. MP4, PDF and GIF are among the formats that play on any digital device, so all three are correct.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST distinguishes traditional artwork from digital art?
options: Traditional artwork uses colour, whereas digital art uses only black and white.
Digital art cannot be printed, whereas traditional artwork can.
Traditional artwork exists as a unique tangible original that is difficult to modify, whereas digital art exists as files that are easy to edit.
Traditional artwork is always older than digital art.
questions.explain: The syllabus contrasts physical, unique, permanent, hand-crafted traditional artwork with electronic, editable digital art made with digital tools. Option D is tempting because traditional art came first historically, but age is not a defining feature: a painting made today is still traditional artwork.

questions.stem: A smartphone now serves as a camera, music player, television, wallet and telephone. This is an example of
questions.explain: Convergence is the coming together of separate media and technologies on one device or platform. Content integration is tempting, but it refers to combining content from different sources into one product, not combining functions on one device.

questions.stem: Admiralty Bay Yacht Club in Bequia wants its logo to look sharp on a 3-metre banner and on a small app icon. Which file format is MOST appropriate for the master logo?
questions.explain: SVG is a vector format, so the logo can scale to any size without losing quality. JPEG is tempting because it is common, but it is a lossy raster format that becomes blurred or blocky when enlarged.

questions.stem: A student's video calls with a tutor in Barbados keep freezing, although her connection speed test shows 150 Mbps. Which term BEST explains the likely cause?
questions.explain: Latency is delay. Real-time calls freeze when delay is high, even with plenty of bandwidth. Low bandwidth is tempting, but the test shows 150 Mbps, which is ample capacity.

questions.stem: Which stage of the web is described as the Read-Write or Social Web?
questions.explain: Web 2.0 introduced user-generated content, social media and interaction. Web 3.0 is tempting because it is also interactive, but it is defined by semantic understanding of data and decentralisation.

questions.stem: A wearable device notices a user's stress level from her heart rate and voice and suggests a calming playlist. This feature is MOST closely linked to which stage of the web?
questions.explain: Web 5.0, the Emotional or Unseen Web, describes systems that sense and respond to human emotions. Web 3.0 is tempting because machines understand meaning, but sensing emotion goes beyond the semantic web.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a BARRIER to equal access to digital media?
options: Assistive technology such as screen readers
Geography, such as remote interior villages
questions.explain: Geography is listed with cost, disability, infrastructure, language, education, age and socio-economic status as a barrier. Assistive technology is tempting because it relates to disability, but it is an enabler that reduces the barrier.

questions.stem: Grenada Spice Trail project produces an interactive map showing nutmeg production by parish, with charts that update each harvest. This product is BEST classified as
questions.explain: Interactive maps, dashboards and charts are data and information design. Animation is tempting because the charts change, but updating figures does not make a product animation.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST explains a difference between mobile phone apps and tablet apps?
options: Tablet apps often use the larger screen for split views, drawing and reading.
Tablet apps cannot be downloaded from app stores.
Phone apps cannot connect to the Internet.
questions.explain: Tablet apps exploit larger screens and often support styluses and keyboards; phone apps are designed for small portrait screens and quick one-handed tasks. The other options are false statements about both device types.

questions.stem: A Lower Six student with no budget needs to edit a podcast and remove background noise. Which tool is MOST appropriate?
questions.explain: Audacity is free, open-source audio editing software with noise reduction. Inkscape is tempting because it is also free and open source, but it is a vector graphics tool, not an audio editor.

questions.stem: In a digital media workflow, which activity is MOST likely to come immediately after writing the creative brief?
questions.explain: After the brief sets purpose and audience, you plan and storyboard or wireframe before creating assets. Publishing is tempting because some think a brief is the last step before release, but asset creation, editing, exporting and accessibility checks come first.

questions.stem: In the technology adoption lifecycle, a respected market vendor who adopts a payment app early and persuades others to follow is BEST described as
options: a member of the late majority
questions.explain: Early adopters are opinion leaders who adopt early and influence others. Innovator is tempting, but innovators are risk-takers who try technology first, often before it is proven, and are not usually the main influencers.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a characteristic of organisations that successfully adopt digital media?
options: Posting the same content on every platform without planning
questions.explain: Successful adopters plan strategically, understand their audience, keep content consistent, use data, act ethically and adapt workflows. Unplanned posting everywhere is the opposite of strategic planning, even though it may look like "consistency".

questions.stem: The decline of printed telephone directories after the growth of search engines and online maps is an example of
questions.explain: An industry became outdated (antiquated) when a digital alternative disrupted it. Content curation is tempting because search engines organise information, but curation describes selecting and sharing content, not an industry's decline.

questions.stem: A graphic designer in Nevis works from home for clients in Canada, the UK and Trinidad, is self-employed and wins work by showing her online portfolio. Which work models does this BEST illustrate?
options: Freelancing, remote work and portfolio-based employment
questions.explain: She is self-employed with many clients (freelancing), works away from an office (remote work) and is hired on her portfolio. Telecommuting is tempting, but it usually describes an employee of one organisation working from home.

questions.stem: Which statement CORRECTLY distinguishes open source software from public domain works?
options: Public domain works must always be credited, whereas open source software never needs a licence.
Open source software is always free of cost, whereas public domain works must be paid for.
Open source software is copyrighted and shared under a licence, whereas public domain works have no copyright protection.
questions.explain: Open source code is still copyrighted; its licence grants freedoms with conditions. Public domain works have no copyright. Option D is the common misconception the syllabus wants you to avoid.

questions.stem: A student remixes an illustration licensed CC BY-SA. Which condition MUST she meet?
options: She must pay a royalty for each use.
She must credit the creator and release her remix under the same licence.
She may use it only for commercial purposes.
She must not change the illustration at all.
questions.explain: BY requires attribution and SA requires adaptations to carry the same licence. Option D describes ND (NoDerivatives), which is not part of this licence.

questions.stem: The Digital Library of the Caribbean provides free online access to Caribbean newspapers and documents. This is BEST described as an example of
questions.explain: Making scholarly and cultural material freely available online is open access. DRM is tempting because a library manages digital content, but DRM restricts access, which is the opposite of what is described.

questions.stem: Which reason BEST explains why Caribbean-centric content creation is important in the context of digital media?
options: It allows creators to avoid copyright law.
It guarantees higher advertising income than international content.
It removes the need for platform considerations.
It represents Caribbean identity, language and lived experience, meets local needs and creates global opportunities.
questions.explain: Caribbean-centric content matters for representation, meeting local and regional needs and global opportunities. Option B is tempting, but small local markets are actually a barrier to advertising income; nothing guarantees higher income.

questions.stem: Tortola Arts Council wants to publish 40-minute interviews with local artists that people can listen to while driving. Which platform type is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Long-form audio for listening on the move suits podcasts. A short-video platform is tempting because it reaches young audiences, but it is designed for short visual clips, not 40-minute audio.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a valid platform consideration?
options: The colour of the platform's logo
The number of letters in the platform's name
questions.explain: Platform considerations are target audience, accessibility, file specifications, algorithms, data privacy, moderation, copyright, terms of service and Caribbean market access. The other options do not affect whether a platform suits a message.

questions.stem: A chatbot gives a student a confident answer that includes a quotation from a Caribbean prime minister that was never said. This is an example of
questions.explain: A hallucination is false or invented information presented as fact by generative AI. Personalisation is tempting because the answer was tailored to the student, but the problem is that the content is invented.

questions.stem: An advertising agency licenses a photograph for one billboard campaign in Kingston for six months only. This is BEST described as
questions.explain: Rights-managed licences are priced for a specific use, place and time. Royalty-free is tempting because both are paid licences, but royalty-free allows many uses for one fee.

questions.stem: Which of the following is protected by a PATENT rather than by copyright?
options: A new device that converts wave energy into electricity
questions.explain: Patents protect new, inventive inventions with industrial application. The song, vlog and photograph are creative works, which copyright protects automatically.

questions.stem: A student downloads a cracked copy of expensive editing software from a file-sharing site. Which statement BEST describes the ethical and practical consequences?
options: It is public domain use because the file was shared freely.
It is piracy and may expose the student's computer to malware, creating security threats and vulnerabilities.
It is fair dealing because it is for school work.
It is acceptable because the software is too costly to buy.
questions.explain: Downloading cracked software is piracy, and such files often carry malware. Option C is tempting because school work sounds educational, but fair dealing covers limited use for purposes such as study or review, not copying an entire commercial program.

questions.stem: Saba Sound Studio compresses its podcast episodes using AAC and its video interviews using H.264 so that they stream smoothly. AAC and H.264 are examples of
questions.explain: A codec (coder-decoder) is software that compresses and decompresses audio or video; AAC and H.264 are codecs. File extensions (.mp4, .m4a) are tempting because the files carry them, but an extension only names the container, not the method of compression.

questions.stem: A hardware store in Montego Bay adds WhatsApp ordering only after many customers complain that every competitor already offers it. In the technology adoption lifecycle, the store is MOST likely part of the
questions.explain: The late majority (34%) adopts when it becomes necessary, often because of customer pressure, as here. The early majority is tempting, but that group adopts once benefits are proven, without waiting until customers are complaining.

questions.stem: Heritage Trust of Nevis creates an app that lets visitors point a phone at the ruins of a sugar estate and see the buildings as they stood in 1800, overlaid on the real view. Using the nine types, this product is BEST classified as
questions.explain: The app responds in real time and overlays digital content on the real world (augmented reality), which places it in interactive and immersive media. Photography and imaging is tempting because a camera is used, but the product's purpose is to let the user explore an experience, not to capture or edit a still image.

questions.stem: A travel agency in Bridgetown has lost many customers to online booking platforms. Which response BEST shows an organisation adapting to disruption?
options: Waiting for customers to return when the platforms become less popular
Cutting prices below those of the global booking platforms
Offering specialist island-hopping packages promoted through its own website, WhatsApp and short videos
Printing more brochures for its shop window
questions.explain: Adapting means using digital media to offer value the disruptor cannot easily match, such as local, specialist packages, and reaching customers where they plan trips. Cutting prices is tempting, but a small agency cannot win a price war against global platforms and would lose money.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes a digital immigrant?
options: A person who has never used digital technology
A person who moved to a new country and uses its internet services
A person who adopted digital technology later in life after learning to work without it
A person who works remotely for an overseas employer
questions.explain: A digital immigrant adopted digital technology later in life. Option B is tempting because of the word "immigrant", but the term is a metaphor about technology, not migration.

questions.stem: Mr. Lake, aged 62, prints every email before replying and phones colleagues to confirm they received his messages. These habits are BEST described as examples of a digital immigrant's
questions.explain: Printing and phoning to confirm are things he does, so they are practices. "Beliefs" is tempting, but beliefs are what he thinks is true, not his behaviour.

questions.stem: A school posts students' photographs and full names on its public social media page without asking permission. Which right of the digital generation is MOST directly affected?
questions.explain: Sharing personal images and names without consent affects privacy. Participation is tempting because students were not consulted, but the main harm is to their personal data.

questions.stem: A user who watches cooking videos and also uploads her own recipe videos is BEST described as a
questions.explain: A prosumer both consumes and produces media. "Consumer" is tempting because she watches videos, but she also produces content.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST definition of the digital media ecosystem?
options: The interconnected network of people, organisations, platforms, technologies and rules through which digital media is created, distributed, consumed and regulated
The hardware used to produce digital media
The set of social media apps on a smartphone
A government department that regulates broadcasting
questions.explain: The ecosystem is the whole interconnected network. Option C is tempting because apps are part of it, but apps alone leave out creators, infrastructure, advertisers and regulators.

questions.stem: In the digital media ecosystem, a company that operates undersea cables and data centres is BEST classified as
questions.explain: Cables and data centres are infrastructure. "Distributor" is tempting because data moves through the cables, but distributors deliver content to outlets or audiences; infrastructure providers supply the networks underneath.

questions.stem: A smartphone that is used as a camera, television, radio, newspaper and telephone is an example of
questions.explain: Convergence is the merging of separate media onto shared devices. Disintermediation is tempting as another "digital change" term, but it refers to removing middlemen from a value chain.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of an emerging trend in which viewers buy products in real time during a broadcast?
questions.explain: Selling during a live broadcast is live commerce. Affiliate marketing is tempting because it involves sales, but it works through links and commission, not real-time broadcasts.

questions.stem: Which sequence shows the core digital media value chain in the CORRECT order?
questions.explain: Content must be created, then produced, then distributed before it earns money. Option C is tempting because production sounds like the start, but the idea (creation) comes first.

questions.stem: A Jamaican reggae artist releases songs directly to fans through a streaming distributor instead of signing with a record label. The removal of the label from the value chain is called
questions.explain: Removing a middleman is disintermediation. Globalisation is tempting because the songs can reach the world, but the question asks about removing the label.

questions.stem: Why does a large video-sharing platform become MORE attractive to advertisers as it gains users?
options: Reintermediation removes the platform from the value chain
More users reduce the cost of infrastructure to zero
Network effects: more users attract more creators and advertisers, increasing the platform's value
Regulators require advertisers to use the largest platform
questions.explain: This is a network effect. Option A is tempting because it uses a value-chain term, but reintermediation means a new middleman appearing, not disappearing.

questions.stem: Pelican Motion cannot deliver a client's video because a storm has cut its internet connection, so the client's advertising campaign is delayed. This BEST illustrates
options: interdependence of players in the ecosystem
questions.explain: A failure in one player (the network) affects others (the studio and client): interdependence. The creator economy is tempting because a studio is involved, but it does not explain the chain reaction.
