questions.stem: A Grenadian student earns small payments by tagging thousands of images online for an AI company, a few cents per task. This is an example of
questions.explain: Tiny tasks for small payments are micro work. Telecommuting is tempting because she works from home, but telecommuting describes working away from an office, not the size or payment of tasks.

questions.stem: Which characteristic of the modern digital media work environment is MOST directly caused by the rapid rate of technological advancement?
questions.explain: When tools change quickly, skills date, so continuous learning is essential. "Fewer global clients" is tempting only if you confuse technology with market size; technology has actually widened access to clients.

questions.stem: A designer in Castries works for clients in Toronto and London, but must compete on price with designers worldwide. This situation BEST illustrates
questions.explain: Global clients and global competition are both effects of globalisation. The digital divide is tempting because it is a regional issue, but the designer clearly has access.

questions.stem: In a PEST analysis of a Caribbean streaming start-up, "high import duties on cameras and editing computers" is BEST classified as
questions.explain: Import duties are set by government policy and raise costs, so the factor is policy and economic. Technological is tempting because cameras are technology, but the issue is their cost and the law, not the technology itself.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST example of an OPPORTUNITY for the Caribbean digital media industry?
options: Global audience interest in Caribbean music, food and culture
questions.explain: Global interest in Caribbean culture is an opportunity. The other options are regional challenges named in the syllabus; small advertising budgets may seem neutral but limit income.

questions.stem: A national emergency office live-streams press briefings, runs a WhatsApp broadcast list and invites residents to report blocked roads online. This is an example of
questions.explain: Informing and involving citizens through digital channels is public engagement. Reintermediation is tempting because WhatsApp is a platform, but the purpose here is engagement, not a change in a value chain.

questions.stem: Flying Fish Films borrows BBD 20,000 from a credit union and repays it with interest over three years, keeping full ownership. This is
questions.explain: Borrowing and repaying with interest is debt financing. Equity is the most tempting distractor, but equity involves giving up ownership, which did not happen.

questions.stem: An early-stage app start-up with no income, high growth potential and a need for mentoring would MOST appropriately seek funding from
options: a venture capitalist or angel investor
questions.explain: Equity investors suit early, high-growth ideas and often provide mentoring. A bank overdraft is tempting because it is easy to get, but repayments without income are very risky.

questions.stem: A photographer receives a fee each time a tourism board uses one of her drone clips. This creator income model is
questions.explain: Being paid for others' use of your content is licensing. Affiliate marketing is tempting as another fee-based model, but it pays commission on sales through your link.

questions.stem: In a project proposal, which section should contain the statement "A survey of 150 residents found that 60% did not know where their nearest hurricane shelter is"?
questions.explain: Evidence that a need exists belongs in the problem statement. Appendices is tempting because the full survey goes there, but the key finding is used in the problem statement.

questions.stem: Which of the following objectives is the MOST appropriate for a project proposal?
options: Make the school more popular online.
Use social media in a better way.
Create some videos for the website soon.
By 30 November, publish four 60-second videos and increase website visits by 20%.
questions.explain: Option D is SMART: specific, measurable and time-bound. Option C is tempting because it mentions videos and timing, but "some" and "soon" cannot be measured.

questions.stem: In the agile project management model, which phase involves evaluating completed work, gathering feedback and comparing actual spending with the planned budget?
questions.explain: Review is defined in exactly these terms. Delivery is tempting because it also reviews costs, but delivery reviews total costs at the end, after the project is finalised.

questions.stem: A pitch for a mobile game states: "The game is free to download, with optional in-app purchases of USD 0.99." Which of the 4Ps does this address?
questions.explain: What customers pay, including a free-with-purchases model, is price. Place is tempting because downloads come from an app store, but this statement is about cost, not the channel.

questions.stem: Which of the following lists the stages of the creative design process in the correct order?
options: Ideation, acceptance, analysis, selection, definition, implementation, evaluation
Acceptance, definition, analysis, ideation, implementation, selection, evaluation
Acceptance, analysis, definition, ideation, selection, implementation, evaluation
Analysis, acceptance, ideation, definition, selection, evaluation, implementation
questions.explain: The sequence is acceptance, analysis, definition, ideation, selection, implementation, evaluation. Option B is tempting because it starts correctly, but definition cannot come before analysis: you must research the problem before you can state it precisely.

questions.stem: A design team in Grenada writes: "Small farmers in St. Andrew need affordable ways to sell produce directly to hotels because 8 of 12 interviewed lose income through middlemen. Success means 30% of them make one direct sale a month." At which stage of the creative design process is the team working?
questions.explain: A precise problem statement with evidence and a success criterion is produced at the definition stage. Ideation is tempting because the statement prepares for ideas, but it contains no ideas or solutions yet.

questions.stem: Which idea generation technique involves writing continuously for a fixed time without stopping to edit or judge?
questions.explain: Free writing is non-stop writing for a set time. Word association is tempting because it also produces words rapidly, but it builds a chain of single linked words rather than continuous text.

questions.stem: In digital media, ideation is BEST defined as
options: generating and developing many possible ideas or concepts for a media product
choosing the final design from a shortlist
exporting a product in a suitable format
questions.explain: Ideation is the generation and development of ideas. Option B is tempting because it follows ideation, but choosing one idea is selection, a converging activity.

questions.stem: A video production company sends each stage of a client's project (script, storyboard, rough cut) for approval, and any rejected stage is revised before the next begins. This is an example of which implementation model?
questions.explain: The work moves forward step by step with review checkpoints that can send a single step back, which is the stepped model with feedback loops. Cyclic is tempting because work is revisited, but in a cyclic model the whole process repeats rather than one step at a checkpoint.

questions.stem: A campaign for a Barbados music festival requires a video, a website and a set of posters, each developed at the same time by a different sub-team and launched together. Which implementation model is being used?
questions.explain: Parallel streams that are later combined form a branched network. Stepped is tempting because each sub-team may follow steps, but the defining feature here is that the work splits into simultaneous branches.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of agile (scrum) project management rather than a linear (waterfall) approach?
options: The client sees the product only at final delivery.
Each phase is completed once and never revisited.
All requirements are fixed before production starts.
Work is delivered in short sprints and priorities are adjusted after each review.
questions.explain: Agile delivers in short sprints and adapts to feedback. The other options describe the linear model; option C is tempting because agile teams also plan, but they do not fix all requirements up front.

questions.stem: A designer wants to show a client the intended colours, textures, fonts and photo style for a new Caribbean skincare brand before any design work begins. Which planning artefact is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: A mood board communicates look and feel. A wireframe is tempting because it is also a planning artefact, but it shows the layout of screens, not colours and textures.

questions.stem: A team designing a market app in St. Lucia asks vendors to test paper sketches and changes button sizes after older vendors struggle to tap them. This BEST illustrates
questions.explain: Involving users and changing the design in response to their abilities is user-centred design. Designing for future needs is tempting because good design lasts, but this decision responds to current users rather than anticipating future change.

questions.stem: Designers are often reminded that "the user is sometimes right". This means that designers should
options: listen to users' needs but also use judgement to design for future needs
always build exactly what users ask for
ignore users and trust their own vision
only design for users who are experts
questions.explain: Users know their problems well, but designers must also anticipate needs users cannot yet imagine. Option B is tempting because user input matters, but users do not always know the best future solution.

questions.stem: Which research method would BEST reveal how fishers in Jamaica actually check sea conditions before going out, rather than what they say they do?
options: A focus group held in town
questions.explain: Observation shows real behaviour in context. A survey is tempting because it reaches many fishers, but it records what people say they do, which can differ from what they actually do.

questions.stem: Which document gives permission for an identifiable person to appear in a published video?
questions.explain: A talent or model release covers the person. A location release is tempting because it is also a clearance, but it covers private property, not people.

questions.stem: A student plans to interview two 15-year-old netball players for a school documentary. Which clearance is REQUIRED before publishing?
options: Releases signed by each student's parent or guardian
Releases signed by the students themselves
questions.explain: Minors cannot give valid consent alone; a parent or guardian must sign. Option B is tempting because the students agreed, but their signatures alone are not enough.

questions.stem: A photographer places the horizon on the lower third line and positions a fishing boat where two third lines cross. Which technique is being applied?
questions.explain: Placing key elements on the third lines and their intersections is the rule of thirds. Symmetry is tempting as a composition technique, but symmetrical images centre the subject rather than placing it on thirds.

questions.stem: In three-point lighting, the light placed behind the subject to separate it from the background is the
questions.explain: The back light (rim or hair light) separates subject from background. The fill light is tempting, but it sits in front, opposite the key, to soften shadows.

questions.stem: An interview recorded indoors under ordinary tungsten bulbs looks orange. Which setting would MOST likely correct this at the time of recording?
options: Setting white balance to about 3200 K
Increasing the frame rate to 60 fps
questions.explain: Tungsten light is about 3200 K, so matching white balance removes the orange cast. Lowering ISO is tempting because it improves image quality, but it affects brightness and noise, not colour.

questions.stem: A heritage society wants a logo that will appear on business cards, T-shirts and a large banner without losing sharpness. Which type of tool and format is MOST suitable?
options: A vector editor saving SVG or PDF
questions.explain: Vector graphics scale to any size without losing quality. A raster editor is tempting because it can also create logos, but raster images blur or pixelate when enlarged.

questions.stem: Which criterion is MOST directly involved when a student finds that 4K editing software runs extremely slowly on a laptop with 4 GB of RAM?
questions.explain: RAM, processor and graphics card limits are technical requirements. Cost is tempting because upgrading would cost money, but the immediate issue is the hardware the software needs.

questions.stem: A tourism office in Aruba posts a beach-status map using only red and green dots. Which accessibility problem does this create?
options: The file size is too large.
It does not have a call to action.
It relies on colour alone, which colour-blind users may not distinguish.
questions.explain: Relying on colour alone excludes colour-blind users; labels or icons should be added. Option C is tempting because good posts have a call to action, but that is not an accessibility issue.

questions.stem: A group must let a client add notes to a cloud-based script without changing the text. Which permission setting is MOST appropriate?
options: Anyone with the link can edit
questions.explain: Commenter allows notes without editing. Editor is tempting because the client is important, but editors can change the text.

questions.stem: For speech recorded for a video project, which combination of settings is MOST appropriate?
questions.explain: 48 kHz matches video standards, 24-bit gives headroom, and peaks of -12 to -6 dBFS avoid clipping. Option C is tempting because 44.1 kHz/16-bit is a valid music standard, but -40 dBFS is far too quiet and will raise noise when boosted.

questions.stem: A student must print an A5 flyer (about 5.8 x 8.3 inches) for a church fundraiser in Antigua. Which specification is MOST appropriate?
questions.explain: Professional print uses CMYK at 300 DPI, delivered as PDF with bleed. Option D is tempting because PNG is high quality, but RGB at 72 DPI is a screen specification and will print soft.

questions.stem: Which export setting is MOST suitable for a promotional clip to be posted on Instagram Reels?
questions.explain: Reels are vertical 9:16, and MP4 with H.264 is widely compatible. Option A is tempting because it is high quality, but ProRes files are very large and 16:9 does not fill a vertical screen.

questions.stem: Which statement about JPEG and PNG is CORRECT?
options: PNG is always smaller than JPEG for photographs.
JPEG uses lossy compression; PNG uses lossless compression and supports transparency.
JPEG supports transparency; PNG does not.
questions.explain: JPEG is lossy and suits photographs; PNG is lossless and supports transparent backgrounds. Option D is tempting because both are common web formats, but it reverses the facts: PNG supports transparency, JPEG does not.

questions.stem: A CAPE student's SBA portfolio contains only the final video. Which addition would MOST improve it as evidence of the design process?
options: A longer version of the same video
Research findings, mind maps, storyboards, a feedback log and an evaluation against success criteria
questions.explain: A digital proposal portfolio must show the process from research to final solution. Option D is tempting because quality matters, but a better export still shows nothing of the research, planning or iteration.

questions.stem:
The Sol Studio in Paramaribo runs both a painting class and a digital illustration class. Sort each description.

Does this describe traditional artwork or digital art?

A watercolour of the Waterkant painted on paper with brushes.
questions.explain: Physical materials and manual technique make this traditional artwork.

questions.stem:
Does this describe traditional artwork or digital art?

A character drawn on a tablet with a stylus in Krita.
questions.explain: It is created with digital tools and exists as a file, so it is digital art.

questions.stem:
Does this describe traditional artwork or digital art?

A mistake can be removed with one click of Undo.
questions.explain: Easy editing (undo and refine) is a key feature of digital art.

questions.stem:
Does this describe traditional artwork or digital art?

There is only one original, which the buyer can hang on a wall.
questions.explain: A unique, tangible original is a feature of traditional artwork.

questions.stem:
Does this describe traditional artwork or digital art?

A charcoal sketch where every line is permanent.
questions.explain: Changes to physical media are hard to reverse, which is a feature of traditional artwork.

questions.stem:
Does this describe traditional artwork or digital art?

A logo saved as an SVG file and sent by email.
questions.explain: It exists in electronic form as a digital file, so it is digital art.

questions.stem:
Does this describe traditional artwork or digital art?

A clay sculpture of a pelican shaped by hand.
questions.explain: It is hand-crafted from physical material, so it is traditional artwork.

questions.stem:
Does this describe traditional artwork or digital art?

A collage built from layers of scanned photos in GIMP.
questions.explain: Layered editing in software makes this digital art, even though the photos were scanned.

questions.stem:
Kareem is setting up media for his family's guesthouse website in Ocho Rios, Jamaica. Answer each question.

He needs the guesthouse logo to stay sharp on a business card and on a large banner. Which type of graphic?
questions.explain: Vector graphics are built from paths, so they scale to any size without losing quality.

questions.stem: His video calls with guests freeze even though his plan is 100 Mbps. The most likely issue is...
questions.explain: Bandwidth is fine; the delay (latency) is the problem. Real-time calls need low latency.

questions.stem: He saves a photo as JPEG and notices slight blurring after repeated saves. This is because JPEG uses...
questions.explain: JPEG discards data each time it compresses, so quality drops with repeated saves.

questions.stem: He wants a logo with a transparent background for the website header, with no quality loss.
questions.explain: PNG is lossless and supports transparency. JPEG cannot store transparency.

questions.stem: He removes the GPS location from photos of his family's home before posting. He is removing...
questions.explain: Location is metadata stored inside the file. Removing it protects privacy.

questions.stem: A video for Instagram Reels should use which aspect ratio?
questions.explain: Vertical short video uses 9:16. 16:9 is landscape, for YouTube and TV.

questions.stem: Trinidad Carnival Live channel sends one video stream of a band's parade to thousands of viewers at the same time, using far less bandwidth than sending each viewer a separate copy. Which term BEST describes this method of delivery?

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem: A Jamaican tourism website in 1998 showed static pages with text, a few photos and an email address. Visitors could read the information but could not comment, upload content or interact with other users. Which stage of the web does this BEST represent?
options: Web 2.0, the Read-Write or Social Web

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem:
The Guyana Rural Learning Network wants to deliver online classes to students in the interior. Sort each factor.

Does this factor enable access or create a barrier?

Lower-cost Android smartphones are now sold in village shops.
questions.explain: Cheaper devices put access within reach of more families.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem:
Does this factor enable access or create a barrier?

Many villages have no reliable electricity supply.
questions.explain: Poor infrastructure is a barrier, because devices and routers need power.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem:
Does this factor enable access or create a barrier?

A free public Wi-Fi hotspot at the community centre.
questions.explain: Public Wi-Fi removes the cost of data for users nearby.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem:
Does this factor enable access or create a barrier?

Mobile data costs a large share of a family's weekly income.
questions.explain: Cost and socio-economic status are major barriers.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem:
Does this factor enable access or create a barrier?

Video lessons include captions and a screen-reader-friendly transcript.
questions.explain: Assistive features make content accessible to students with disabilities.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem:
Does this factor enable access or create a barrier?

Some grandparents caring for students have never used a smartphone.
questions.explain: Age and low digital literacy can be barriers.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem:
Does this factor enable access or create a barrier?

Long distances and rivers make it hard to install towers.
questions.explain: Geography is a barrier to building infrastructure.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem:
Does this factor enable access or create a barrier?

A digital literacy workshop for parents at the school.
questions.explain: Digital literacy training helps people use the technology they have.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem:
You are advising St. Kitts Heritage Trust, which wants to launch a digital guide to historic sites for residents and visitors. Make the best decisions.

The Trust's board wants a cutting-edge VR headset experience at each site. Many residents use only basic smartphones with limited data. What do you advise first?
options: Research the audience's devices, data costs and skills before choosing the technology.
Buy the VR headsets now; new technology always attracts users.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem: Your research shows most users have mid-range smartphones and pay for data by the day. Which format do you recommend?
options: A lightweight mobile web guide with short audio clips and an option to download content on free Wi-Fi.
Large 4K 360-degree videos that stream only over fast connections.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem: Before launch, a board member asks whether anything else could limit adoption. What do you add?
options: Nothing. Anyone who wants it will work it out.
Captions, transcripts and a simple interface, plus QR codes at each site and a short workshop at the library for older residents.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem: A student in Barbados makes a zoetrope: 12 drawings of a bouncing ball on a paper strip inside a spinning drum. Which statement BEST explains why viewers see one moving ball?
options: The paper strip is coated with chemicals that change the drawings as the drum spins.
The drawings are digital, so the computer fills in the frames between them.
The images follow one another so quickly that the eye and brain blend them into continuous motion, the effect known as persistence of vision.
The drum projects the drawings onto a wall with a lamp, like a magic lantern.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem:
Sort each moving-image technology according to whether it is analogue or digital.

Analogue or digital?

35 mm film negative developed in chemicals
questions.explain: Physical film with a chemical image is analogue.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem:
Analogue or digital?

Cutting and taping film strips together on a Steenbeck editing table
questions.explain: Physical cutting is linear, analogue editing.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem:
Analogue or digital?

Editing in DaVinci Resolve, moving clips freely on a timeline
questions.explain: Software editing is digital, non-linear editing (NLE).

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem:
Analogue or digital?

A VHS cassette recorded from television
questions.explain: VHS stores a continuous magnetic signal: analogue.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem:
Analogue or digital?

A cinema projecting a Digital Cinema Package (DCP) from a server
questions.explain: A DCP is a set of digital files.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem:
Analogue or digital?

A zoetrope strip of hand-drawn frames
questions.explain: Drawings on paper viewed mechanically: analogue.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem:
Analogue or digital?

Computer-generated dinosaurs rendered frame by frame
questions.explain: CGI is created as digital data.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem:
Analogue or digital?

A film watched on a streaming app at 1080p
questions.explain: Streaming delivers compressed digital data.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem: At a Nevis resort, sensors detect when a guest leaves the room and switch off the air conditioning. The guest's AI agent sees a flight delay in real time and automatically moves the airport taxi. Which statement BEST classifies this system?
options: Web 5.0, because the system responds to the guest's needs.
Web 3.0, because it uses AI to personalise information.
Web 4.0, because intelligent connected systems combine IoT sensors, AI and real-time data, and act as a partner for the guest.
Web 2.0, because the guest interacts with the resort online.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem:
Read each description and choose the Web generation it BEST represents.

A Barbados bakery's 1999 website shows opening hours and a map. To order, you phone the shop.
questions.explain: Static and read-only: Web 1.0.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem: Trinidad and Tobago Carnival fans upload thousands of videos and comment on each other's costumes.
questions.explain: User-generated content and two-way communication: Web 2.0.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem: A search tool understands "family-friendly beach in Jamaica with lifeguards" and gives one direct, personalised answer.
questions.explain: Understanding meaning and personalising with AI: the semantic Web 3.0.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem: Sensors on Seven Mile Beach in Grand Cayman send live water-quality data to a public map and to residents' smartwatches.
questions.explain: IoT sensors, real-time data and connected devices: Web 4.0.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem: A tutoring app reads a student's facial expression, notices frustration and slows down the lesson.
questions.explain: Responding to emotion: the emotional Web 5.0.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem: A Jamaican musician sells a limited digital edition of a song on a blockchain, with no record label in between.
questions.explain: Decentralised ownership through blockchain is the "decentralised" side of Web 3.0.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem:
A Jamaican youth radio station is moving online. Some of these factors are trickier than they look. Sort each one.

Does this factor help people get access, or block it?

The island relies on very few submarine cables, so one cable fault slows the whole island.
questions.explain: Few cables means little redundancy: an infrastructure and geography barrier.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem:
Does this factor help people get access, or block it?

A second submarine cable route is added, so traffic can switch if one is cut.
questions.explain: Redundancy makes connectivity more reliable: an enabler.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem:
Does this factor help people get access, or block it?

Every video on the station's site has accurate captions and a transcript.
questions.explain: Captions and transcripts support deaf and hard-of-hearing users: accessible design.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem:
Does this factor help people get access, or block it?

The station's app is only in English, but many listeners prefer Kwéyòl.
questions.explain: Language is a recognised barrier to access.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem:
Does this factor help people get access, or block it?

Photos on the website have alt text that a screen reader can read aloud.
questions.explain: Alt text lets blind and partially sighted users understand images.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem:
Does this factor help people get access, or block it?

After a hurricane, a cell tower is out of action for three weeks.
questions.explain: Hurricane damage to infrastructure is a major Caribbean barrier.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem:
Does this factor help people get access, or block it?

The library offers free evening classes on using streaming apps for older residents.
questions.explain: Digital literacy training tackles age and education barriers.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem:
Does this factor help people get access, or block it?

A prepaid data bundle large enough for daily streaming costs a big share of a student's allowance.
questions.explain: Cost is a barrier, especially for low-income households.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem:
You are advising the Richardson family, who run a small bakery and catering business in St. Lucia. They want more online orders, but many of their customers are older, some live in areas with weak signal, and data is expensive for some families.

The family's nephew wants a large website with HD video, 3D product views and an AI chatbot. What do you advise first?
options: Find out how customers actually get online: which devices, which apps, how much data, and who struggles.
Build the big site now: modern customers expect the latest features.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem: Your survey shows most customers use WhatsApp on mid-range phones, many buy small daily data bundles, and older customers prefer to phone. Which channel plan do you recommend?
options: Close phone orders and take orders only through a new app customers must download.
A WhatsApp Business catalogue with small, compressed photos, a lightweight one-page site, and the phone number kept on everything.

questions.topic: Evolution of digital media and future trends
questions.stem: A hurricane warning is issued, and a customer with a visual impairment says she cannot read the menu images. What do you add?
options: Nothing more: the menu images look attractive, and hurricanes are rare.
A text version of the menu that screen readers can read, alt text on photos, and a plan to post updates by SMS and local radio if the Internet goes down.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
The Tobago Festival Committee is planning its digital media for the season. Classify each product.

Which group of digital media does each product belong to?

A weekly podcast interviewing steelpan arrangers.
questions.explain: A podcast is digital audio.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which group of digital media does each product belong to?

A 30-second animated sponsor logo.
questions.explain: Animated logo design is animation and motion graphics.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which group of digital media does each product belong to?

A 360-degree virtual tour of Fort King George.
questions.explain: Virtual tours are interactive and immersive media.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which group of digital media does each product belong to?

Retouched and restored photos from the 1970s festival.
questions.explain: Retouching and restoration are digital photography and imaging.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which group of digital media does each product belong to?

Custom sound effects for the festival app.
questions.explain: Sound effects are digital audio.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which group of digital media does each product belong to?

An AR game where visitors find hidden masks around Scarborough.
questions.explain: AR games respond to the user and blend digital content with the real world.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which group of digital media does each product belong to?

A projection-mapping show on the walls of a historic building.
questions.explain: Projection mapping is listed under interactive and immersive media.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which group of digital media does each product belong to?

An audiobook of Tobago folk tales.
questions.explain: Audiobooks are digital audio.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which group of digital media does each product belong to?

Concept art for the festival's new mascot character.
questions.explain: Concept art and character design are digital art.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Nadia is a Lower Six student in Jamaica planning her SBA. Choose the best option each time.

She has no budget and needs to remove background noise from interview recordings.
questions.explain: Audacity is free, open source and has noise reduction. Canva is not an audio editor.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem: She needs a logo that will print on T-shirts and appear on a website.
options: a vector tool such as Inkscape
questions.explain: Vector tools produce scalable logos suitable for print and web.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem: Her group of three needs to edit the proposal at the same time from home.
options: a cloud collaboration tool such as Google Docs
questions.explain: Cloud collaboration allows real-time co-editing from different locations.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem: Before building her app, she wants users to click through the screens and give feedback.
options: a prototyping tool such as Figma
questions.explain: App prototyping tools create clickable mock-ups for audience testing.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem: Which stage should come straight after writing the creative brief?
questions.explain: After the brief, you plan and storyboard. Publishing and analytics come much later.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Eight Caribbean media products. Use the four questions (purpose, features, production, delivery) to place each in the right type.

Which of the first three major types is each product?

A vector logo for a St. John’s food truck, drawn in Inkscape.
questions.explain: A logo drawn with vector paths is digital art used for branding.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which of the first three major types is each product?

A weekly podcast on Anguilla's salt-pond history.
questions.explain: Recorded speech, edited in a DAW and delivered on podcast apps: digital audio.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which of the first three major types is each product?

A 30-second animated hurricane-preparedness explainer for the Meteorological Department.
questions.explain: Keyframed movement on a timeline that explains a process: animation and motion graphics.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which of the first three major types is each product?

A soca riddim produced in a home studio and released on streaming services.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which of the first three major types is each product?

A digital painting of Fort George made with a tablet and stylus.
questions.explain: Layers and brushes on a tablet produce digital art.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which of the first three major types is each product?

An animated logo sting that opens a Barbados TV newscast.
questions.explain: Moving text and shapes on a timeline: motion graphics.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which of the first three major types is each product?

A Carnival costume concept sheet created in Procreate.
questions.explain: Concept art and costume design are digital art.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which of the first three major types is each product?

A radio jingle for a Trinidad hardware store, with a voiceover and sound effects.
questions.explain: Voice, music and effects mixed for listening: digital audio.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Eight more Caribbean products. Decide which of the next three types each one belongs to.

Which major type is each product?

A bus-arrival app that alerts Kingston commuters when their bus is near.
questions.explain: A touch-screen service with notifications: a mobile app.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which major type is each product?

A smartwatch that shows a runner's pace during the Nevis half-marathon.
questions.explain: The wearable is a device that creates and displays data and media.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which major type is each product?

Restored scans of family photographs damaged in Hurricane Irma.
questions.explain: Scanning and retouching are digital imaging.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which major type is each product?

A mobile quiz game about Caribbean capitals with in-app rewards.
questions.explain: A game with touch interaction and in-app rewards: apps and games.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which major type is each product?

A smart TV in a hotel lobby that plays the resort's welcome video.
questions.explain: The smart TV is the device; content must be exported in 16:9 to suit it.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which major type is each product?

Product photos of Guyanese cassareep jars for an online shop.
questions.explain: Photographs that advertise products: digital photography.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which major type is each product?

A tablet used by a Grenadian artist to draw and present her portfolio.
questions.explain: The tablet is the device used to create, store and show media.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which major type is each product?

A news photographer's images of flooding in Port of Spain, with GPS metadata.
questions.explain: Documenting events with resolution and metadata: digital photography.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
The last eight Caribbean products. Place each one in the right type.

Which major type is each product?

Reels and a live stream from Eagle Beach, Aruba, for a tourism campaign.
questions.explain: Short, frequent platform posts built for reach: social media content.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which major type is each product?

A dashboard of monthly visitor arrivals used by a hotel to plan staffing.
questions.explain: Turning data into decisions: data and information design.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which major type is each product?

A 360° virtual tour of Brimstone Hill Fortress in St. Kitts.
questions.explain: The user controls the view and explores: immersive media.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which major type is each product?

An infographic comparing rainfall in each Jamaican parish.
questions.explain: Accurate data shown with clear labels and colour: data design.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which major type is each product?

A hashtag challenge for a Bajan dance festival.
questions.explain: Hashtags, sharing and algorithm-driven reach: social media content.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which major type is each product?

An AR app that shows a Kalinago village rebuilt on its real site when you point your phone at it.
questions.explain: AR blends digital content with the real world in real time: immersive media.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which major type is each product?

An interactive map with filters showing reef health around Bonaire.
questions.explain: Interactive filters on data still make it data and information design, because its purpose is to clarify data.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem:
Which major type is each product?

A VR safety simulation that trains port workers in Kingston.
questions.explain: A simulated environment that surrounds the user: immersive media.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem: The Holetown Ferry Company designed its new advert as a 1080 × 1080 pixel raster image for Instagram. It now wants the same design on a 6-metre roadside billboard on the Airport Road. What is the BEST advice?
options: Save the Instagram image as a PNG instead of a JPEG, because PNG files can be enlarged without losing quality.
Use the Instagram file as it is, because a billboard is viewed from far away so quality does not matter.
Increase the image size to 20,000 pixels in the photo editor, because this adds the missing detail.
Rebuild the logo and text as vector graphics (for example in Inkscape) and use a high-resolution photo, because raster images lose quality when enlarged while vectors scale without loss.

questions.topic: Types of digital media and the tools that make them
questions.stem: A Trinidad and Tobago environmental group has recorded the amount of plastic collected (in kg) at one beach every month for three years. It wants to show the public whether its campaign is reducing plastic over time. Which chart is MOST appropriate?
options: A scatter plot of kilograms against beach length.
A 3D bar chart starting at 200 kg to make the drop look dramatic.
A pie chart with 36 slices, one for each month.
A line chart with months on the x-axis and kilograms on the y-axis, starting at zero, with the campaign start marked.

Artists in Belize and Toronto now book remote mixing sessions.

questions.topic: Impact of digital media on businesses and organisations

Streaming pays the studio's artists very little per play.

questions.topic: Impact of digital media on businesses and organisations

Is this a benefit or a limitation of digital media for the studio?

questions.topic: Impact of digital media on businesses and organisations

Is this a benefit or a limitation of digital media for the studio?

questions.explain: Dependence on platforms is a limitation.
