questions.stem:
Is this a benefit or a limitation of digital media for the studio?

Short behind-the-scenes clips attract new clients at no cost.
questions.explain: Low-cost marketing is a benefit.

questions.topic: Impact of digital media on businesses and organisations
questions.stem:
Is this a benefit or a limitation of digital media for the studio?

Staff must now manage messages and comments every evening.
questions.explain: Extra workload is a limitation.

questions.topic: Impact of digital media on businesses and organisations
questions.stem:
You are a digital media consultant for the Marigot Bay Dive Centre in St. Lucia. Bookings have fallen while competitors grow online. Make the best decisions.

The owner says, "Just post something every day on every platform." What do you recommend first?
options: Post random photos on every platform immediately.
Set clear goals and research the target audience (divers from North America and Europe aged 25 to 50).

questions.topic: Impact of digital media on businesses and organisations
questions.stem: The audience is found mainly on Instagram, YouTube and travel review sites. How will you manage content?
options: A weekly content calendar with consistent branding: reef videos, safety tips and customer stories.
Copy competitors' videos and post them as your own.

questions.topic: Impact of digital media on businesses and organisations
questions.stem: After two months, analytics show reef videos get five times more engagement than price posts. What next?
options: Shift the plan towards reef videos and add a booking link, then keep reviewing the data.
Ignore the analytics and keep posting price lists.

questions.topic: Impact of digital media on businesses and organisations
questions.stem: In the 1990s, many Caribbean towns had shops that rented videotapes and DVDs. Most have now closed. Which statement BEST explains this change?
options: Video rental shops were early adopters of streaming technology.
On-demand streaming platforms disrupted the rental business model, and shops that did not adapt became antiquated.
Governments banned physical media to protect copyright.
People stopped watching films because social media replaced entertainment.

questions.topic: Impact of digital media on businesses and organisations
questions.stem:
You are a digital media adviser. Bay Street Travel in Kingstown, St. Vincent, has sold flights and island-hopping trips for 25 years. Bookings have fallen by half since customers started booking online. Help the owner, Mrs. Providence, adapt to the disruption.

Mrs. Providence says, "The booking websites are cheaper. Should I just close?" What do you advise first?
options: Identify what the agency offers that big booking sites cannot (local knowledge, personal service, island-hopping packages) and who still needs it, then set clear goals.
Cut all prices below the booking websites to win customers back.

questions.topic: Impact of digital media on businesses and organisations
questions.stem: You find a niche: visitors from cruise ships and Europe who want guided island-hopping to Bequia, Mustique and Union Island, plus local families who want help with complex trips. How should the agency reach them?
options: Print 5,000 brochures and wait for customers to walk in.
A mobile-friendly website with online enquiry, WhatsApp Business for quick replies, and short reels of real trips posted on a regular schedule.

questions.topic: Impact of digital media on businesses and organisations
questions.stem: Three months later, a platform changes its algorithm and reel views drop sharply. Enquiries through the website, however, keep rising. What now?
options: Stop all digital work, because the algorithm proves digital media does not work.
Check the analytics, put more effort into the website and an email list the agency owns, and use several platforms so no single one controls its reach.

questions.stem:
Sort each resource that a Lower Six student in Trinidad might use for her SBA.

Which category best describes each resource?

Audacity, whose code anyone may modify under the GPL.
questions.explain: Software with published, modifiable source code under a licence is open source.

questions.stem:
Which category best describes each resource?

A photo whose creator released it under CC0.
questions.explain: CC0 waives rights and places the work in the public domain.

questions.stem:
Which category best describes each resource?

A Wikipedia article reused with credit under the same licence.
questions.explain: Wikipedia text is licensed CC BY-SA.

questions.stem:
Which category best describes each resource?

A painting whose copyright expired many decades ago.
questions.explain: Expired copyright means the work is in the public domain.

questions.stem:
Which category best describes each resource?

Blender, the free 3D tool with published source code.
questions.explain: Blender is open-source software.

questions.stem:
Which category best describes each resource?

A song on a music site labelled CC BY-NC.
questions.explain: It is a Creative Commons licence with attribution and non-commercial conditions.

questions.stem:
Which category best describes each resource?

WordPress, the website CMS developed by a global volunteer community.
questions.explain: WordPress is open-source software.

questions.stem:
Which category best describes each resource?

An OER textbook chapter marked CC BY 4.0.
questions.explain: It is shared under a Creative Commons licence.

questions.stem: A Barbadian student writes a review of a new soca album for her school's online magazine. She quotes two short lines from one song to support her criticism and names the artist and song. Which statement BEST describes her use?
options: It is likely to be fair dealing, because she uses a small extract for criticism and review and acknowledges the source.
It is open source use, because the magazine is free.
It is public domain use, because the album is available online.
It is infringement, because any quotation without written permission is illegal.

questions.stem: Audacity, Mozilla Firefox, Blender and Torch are all application software. Besides that, what do the first three MOST clearly have in common?
options: They are all made by the same company.
They are all in the public domain, so no licence applies.
They are free to use and their source code is open, so anyone can study, modify and share them: they are open-source software.
They can only be used by programmers.

questions.stem:
A family from Antigua is planning a weekend in St. Kitts. Sort each item from raw data to knowledge.

Is this data, information or knowledge?

"EC$40" on its own.
questions.explain: A price with no context is raw data.

questions.stem:
Is this data, information or knowledge?

A set of GPS co-ordinates.
questions.explain: A location alone is raw data.

questions.stem:
Is this data, information or knowledge?

A single star rating: 4.
questions.explain: One rating with nothing around it is raw data.

questions.stem:
Is this data, information or knowledge?

A page about Brimstone Hill Fortress with its location, photos, entry price and opening hours.
questions.explain: The data has been collected and given context: information about an attraction.

questions.stem:
Is this data, information or knowledge?

A ferry timetable listing departure times, prices and the route to Nevis.
questions.explain: Organised data with context is information.

questions.stem:
Is this data, information or knowledge?

A map showing every beach with its facilities.
questions.explain: Data presented together in context: information.

questions.stem:
Is this data, information or knowledge?

"Grandma cannot walk far, so we will choose beaches with parking close to the sand."
questions.explain: Information applied to the family's needs to make a choice: knowledge.

questions.stem:
Is this data, information or knowledge?

"The children get seasick, so we will skip the ferry and spend Saturday in Basseterre."
questions.explain: A decision based on information and personal needs: knowledge.

questions.stem:
Use the three conditions (availability and access, reuse and redistribution, universal participation) to decide.

A government posts hurricane-shelter locations as a CSV file under a licence that allows any reuse.
questions.explain: Machine-readable, free and licensed for any reuse: open.

questions.stem: A ministry publishes tourist-arrival figures only as a scanned PDF image of a printed table.
questions.explain: A scan is not machine-readable, so it fails the availability condition.

questions.stem: A bus timetable dataset is free to download but licensed "for educational use only".
questions.explain: Restricting who may use it, or what for, breaks universal participation.

questions.stem: A statistics office charges a small fee that covers only the cost of copying a large dataset onto a drive, and lets anyone reuse it commercially.
questions.explain: A fee of no more than the reasonable reproduction cost is acceptable. Free to use does not always mean free to access.

questions.stem: A reef-monitoring group shares its data in JSON format but forbids anyone from combining it with other data.
questions.explain: The licence must allow people to transform and combine the data.

questions.stem:
Students at Calabash Point Secondary in Grenada are making a heritage website. Decide which idea allows each use.

What allows this use?

Using a 1850s map of the island whose copyright expired long ago.
questions.explain: Copyright has expired: public domain.

questions.stem:
What allows this use?

Using a photo marked CC0 by its creator.
questions.explain: CC0 is a public domain dedication.

questions.stem:
What allows this use?

Using a CC BY photo of Fort George, credited to the photographer.
questions.explain: Copyright is retained; the licence grants permission with attribution.

questions.stem:
What allows this use?

Remixing a CC BY-SA illustration and sharing the new version under CC BY-SA.
questions.explain: ShareAlike: the derivative must use the same licence.

questions.stem:
What allows this use?

Quoting two lines of a published poem in a review of the poet's book, with the source acknowledged.
questions.explain: A limited quotation for review is a fair dealing purpose.

questions.stem:
What allows this use?

Copying one short paragraph of a history book for private study.
questions.explain: Private study of a limited amount is a fair dealing purpose.

questions.stem:
What allows this use?

Using a Shakespeare sonnet in full in a poetry video.
questions.explain: Shakespeare's works are in the public domain.

questions.stem:
What allows this use?

Showing a 10-second news clip to criticise how a report covered the island, with credit.
questions.explain: Short use for criticism or news reporting can be fair dealing; it depends on purpose and amount.

questions.stem:
A youth film club in Oranjestad, Aruba, uses open tools and content. Sort each statement.

Is this a benefit of open content or a responsibility of the user?

They edit their film in Blender and Audacity without paying for licences.
questions.explain: Cost reduction is a benefit.

questions.stem:
Is this a benefit of open content or a responsibility of the user?

They credit every CC BY photo with title, author, source and licence.
questions.explain: Attribution is a responsibility.

questions.stem:
Is this a benefit of open content or a responsibility of the user?

Volunteers in three islands improve the same open subtitle file together.
questions.explain: Collaboration is a benefit.

questions.stem:
Is this a benefit of open content or a responsibility of the user?

Because they remixed a CC BY-SA song, they release the remix under CC BY-SA.
questions.explain: Following share-alike requirements is a responsibility.

questions.stem:
Is this a benefit of open content or a responsibility of the user?

They use open government data on visitor numbers to show the impact of tourism.
questions.explain: Transparency and access are benefits.

questions.stem:
Is this a benefit of open content or a responsibility of the user?

They do not use a CC BY-NC clip in a paid advert for a sponsor.
questions.explain: Respecting licence terms (NC) is a responsibility.

questions.stem:
Is this a benefit of open content or a responsibility of the user?

They adapt an open lesson on storyboarding to include Caribbean examples.
questions.explain: Adaptability is a benefit.

questions.stem:
Is this a benefit of open content or a responsibility of the user?

They avoid cropping a CC BY photo in a way that misrepresents the people in it.
questions.explain: Ethical reuse of open content is a responsibility.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem:
You are producing a short video series about the fishing village of Anse Bleu in Dominica for a regional tourism campaign. Make the best decisions.

The client suggests opening with stock footage of a generic white-sand beach and steel drums, even though Anse Bleu has a black-sand beach and is known for its drum and Kweyol songs. What do you do?
options: Film the real village, its black-sand beach and its own music, with residents' permission.
Use the generic stock footage; it looks like what tourists expect.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem: An elder agrees to tell the story of the village's founding in Kweyol. Many viewers will not understand Kweyol. What do you do?
options: Keep her words in Kweyol and add accurate English and French subtitles, checked with a community member.
Ask her to speak in English instead, so it is easier.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem: During filming, you see a private family ceremony on the beach. It would make a powerful shot. What do you do?
options: Film it secretly from a distance; it is a public beach.
Ask the family for permission first, and do not film if they refuse.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem:
Answer each question about Caribbean-centric content.

A Turks and Caicos NGO digitises recordings of elders' stories about the salt industry on Salt Cay. This mainly helps to...
questions.explain: Digitising oral histories preserves cultural heritage for future generations.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem: A Jamaican farmer's YouTube channel in Patois explaining drought-resistant crops mainly...
options: meets local needs through creative communication
questions.explain: It solves a local problem in the audience's own language.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem: Which is a barrier that has slowed digital media in the Caribbean?
questions.explain: Small markets limit local advertising and subscription income.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem: A video about Garifuna culture should be made...
options: with the community's input and consent
without captions to keep it authentic
questions.explain: Ethical representation and cultural sensitivity require the community's involvement.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem: A Trinidadian chef's recipe reels gain followers in London and New York. This shows...
questions.explain: Digital platforms carry Caribbean content to global and diaspora audiences.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem:
A team is making a short video series about Carnival and everyday life in Antigua and Barbuda. Sort each choice.

Is this a good practice to follow (do) or one to avoid (don't)?

Ask each masquerader for consent before filming close-ups.
questions.explain: Consent is part of ethical representation.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem:
Is this a good practice to follow (do) or one to avoid (don't)?

Show only palm trees, cocktails and empty beaches to sum up island life.
questions.explain: That is the "paradise postcard" stereotype; it hides lived experience.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem:
Is this a good practice to follow (do) or one to avoid (don't)?

Add captions in English and Spanish and offer a low-data version.
questions.explain: Accessibility and audience awareness.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem:
Is this a good practice to follow (do) or one to avoid (don't)?

Film a church ceremony and post it without asking the congregation.
questions.explain: Sacred traditions need permission: cultural sensitivity.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem:
Is this a good practice to follow (do) or one to avoid (don't)?

Credit the local band whose music you use, with their permission.
questions.explain: Credit sources and people.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem:
Is this a good practice to follow (do) or one to avoid (don't)?

Use a traditional costume as a joke prop in a comedy sketch.
questions.explain: Symbols used out of context disrespect the culture.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem:
Is this a good practice to follow (do) or one to avoid (don't)?

Interview residents about rebuilding after Hurricane Irma in their own words.
questions.explain: Our voice: lived experience told by the people who lived it.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem:
Is this a good practice to follow (do) or one to avoid (don't)?

Copy a stranger's Carnival photo from social media without credit.
questions.explain: No permission and no credit: unethical.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem:
The activity: Choose, Plan, Check, Pitch. Your team has ten minutes to plan a two-minute pitch. Make the best decision at each step.

Choose. Which theme will you pitch?
options: A copy of a popular American prank channel, filmed in Belize City.
A local need: hurricane-preparedness tips for elderly residents, in English and Spanish.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem: Plan. Who is it for, and which format and platform?
options: Elderly residents and their families: short captioned videos shared on WhatsApp and Facebook, plus a printable infographic.
A 40-minute 4K film on a streaming site that needs a paid subscription.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem: Check. Ethics, accessibility and licences. Which plan do you choose?
options: Get consent from everyone filmed, add large captions, use CC0 icons and edit in open-source tools (Shotcut, GIMP).
Use a famous song from the radio as the soundtrack because everyone knows it.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem:
A creator in Montserrat is checking a platform before publishing. Group each question by the kind of consideration it is.

Which group does each consideration belong to?

Are most of my viewers aged 16 to 25 and on their phones?
options: Rights and rules (copyright, terms, privacy, moderation)
questions.explain: Target audience.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem:
Which group does each consideration belong to?

Can people with hearing loss follow the video?
options: Rights and rules (copyright, terms, privacy, moderation)
questions.explain: Accessibility: captions.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem:
Which group does each consideration belong to?

Can buyers in Antigua and Barbuda pay and receive deliveries through this shop platform?
options: Rights and rules (copyright, terms, privacy, moderation)
questions.explain: Caribbean market access.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem:
Which group does each consideration belong to?

Do I have permission to use this soca track?
options: Rights and rules (copyright, terms, privacy, moderation)
questions.explain: Copyright.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem:
Which group does each consideration belong to?

What may the platform do with my photos once I upload them?
options: Rights and rules (copyright, terms, privacy, moderation)
questions.explain: Terms of service.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem:
Which group does each consideration belong to?

What personal data does the app collect from young users?
options: Rights and rules (copyright, terms, privacy, moderation)
questions.explain: Data privacy.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem:
Which group does each consideration belong to?

Who removes abusive comments under my posts?
options: Rights and rules (copyright, terms, privacy, moderation)
questions.explain: Moderation.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem:
Which group does each consideration belong to?

Does the platform accept 9:16 MP4 files under 60 seconds?
options: Rights and rules (copyright, terms, privacy, moderation)
questions.explain: File specifications.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem:
Which group does each consideration belong to?

Does the feed favour videos watched to the end?
options: Rights and rules (copyright, terms, privacy, moderation)
questions.explain: Algorithms.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem:
The activity: for each situation, choose the best platform type. Then check the consideration that matters most.

A youth group wants to share a short documentary about a local festival.
questions.explain: Video-sharing (or short video on social media) reaches young viewers. Consideration: check copyright on the music.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem: A craft seller wants to sell handmade jewellery to visitors and the diaspora.
questions.explain: An e-commerce platform or CMS-based shop. Consideration: check local payment and delivery options (market access).

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem: A student wants to interview elders about local history for listeners with limited data.
questions.explain: A podcast uses little data and is easy to share through RSS and mobile apps.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem: A teacher wants to run a class with quizzes and assignments online.
questions.explain: A learning platform such as Moodle or Google Classroom. Consideration: privacy of student data and accessibility.

questions.topic: Caribbean-centric content and digital media platforms
questions.stem: For the teacher's class, which consideration matters MOST?
options: How the algorithm ranks viral posts
questions.explain: Students' personal data and grades must be protected.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem:
A Communication and Digital Media club in Barbados is preparing a poster on life online. Sort each card.

Is this an opportunity, a risk or a responsibility?

Taking a free online course in motion graphics.
questions.explain: Online learning is an opportunity.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem:
Is this an opportunity, a risk or a responsibility?

A party photo from Form 3 resurfaces during a job interview.
questions.explain: Permanent records and material discovery are risks.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem:
Is this an opportunity, a risk or a responsibility?

Checking two trusted news sources before sharing a storm warning.
questions.explain: Verification of sources is a responsibility.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem:
Is this an opportunity, a risk or a responsibility?

A message meant as a joke is read as an insult.
questions.explain: Confused text and miscommunication are pitfalls.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem:
Is this an opportunity, a risk or a responsibility?

A small business follows up with customers after each sale.
questions.explain: Customer follow-up is an opportunity.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem:
Is this an opportunity, a risk or a responsibility?

Adding captions so deaf viewers can follow your video.
questions.explain: Accessibility is part of inclusive digital citizenship.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem:
Is this an opportunity, a risk or a responsibility?

A fake online store takes payment and never delivers.
questions.explain: Scams are a risk.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem:
Is this an opportunity, a risk or a responsibility?

Watching parliament live and commenting on a draft law.
questions.explain: Civic participation is an opportunity.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem:
Is this an opportunity, a risk or a responsibility?

Asking a friend before posting a photo of them.
questions.explain: Privacy protection and responsible sharing are responsibilities.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem: During a tropical storm, a political group in a Caribbean territory creates a fake government notice saying the airport is closed for a week, in order to embarrass the government. Thousands of residents then share it, believing it is true. Which statement is MOST accurate?
options: Both the group and the residents spread misinformation.
The group created disinformation; residents who shared it in good faith spread misinformation.
It is a deepfake, because it is false.
Both the group and the residents spread disinformation.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem:
You run the student news page at your sixth form in a Caribbean territory. Two days before a general election, a video appears showing a candidate apparently insulting fishermen. It is spreading fast.

Your followers are asking you to share it. What do you do first?
options: Hold off and verify: check the original source, look for coverage by trusted outlets and examine the video for signs of manipulation.
Share it immediately; people deserve to know.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem: You notice the lips do not match the words, the voice sounds flat, and no news outlet has the original. A fact-checking group says it is likely AI-generated. What now?
options: Repost the clip with "Is this real?" to get engagement.
Post a clear, calm explainer that the video appears to be a deepfake, showing how to spot one, without re-posting the full clip.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem: A classmate suggests making your own AI video of the other candidate "to even things out". What do you say?
options: Sure, but label it as satire in small print.
No. Creating a deepfake of a real person without consent is unethical and could be illegal; we will stick to verified reporting.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem:
Answer each question about AI in digital media.

An AI tool adds automatic captions to a council meeting video. This is mainly a benefit for...
questions.explain: Captions make content accessible to deaf and hard-of-hearing viewers.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem: A chatbot gives a student a reference to a journal article that does not exist. This is...
questions.explain: Inventing false information confidently is a hallucination. Always check AI references.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem: An image generator keeps showing Caribbean markets as run-down and poor. This shows...
questions.explain: Unbalanced training data can produce stereotyped output.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem: A student states in her SBA: "I used an AI tool to suggest titles; I wrote and edited all content myself." This is...
questions.explain: Transparency and acknowledgement are ethical uses of AI.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem: A studio uses AI to resize one poster into ten platform formats in a minute. Industry calls this...
questions.explain: Automating repetitive tasks increases productivity, an industry expectation.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem:
Each item comes from digital life across the Caribbean. Sort it.

Is this an opportunity or a pitfall of digital media?

A Bay Street boutique in Nassau sells to cruise passengers through Instagram before the ship docks.
questions.explain: Reach and economy: an opportunity.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem:
Is this an opportunity or a pitfall of digital media?

Recovery updates after Hurricane Irma reach residents through WhatsApp and radio livestreams.
questions.explain: Crisis communication: an opportunity.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem:
Is this an opportunity or a pitfall of digital media?

A student's offensive post from four years ago resurfaces when she applies for a scholarship.
questions.explain: Digital footprint: a pitfall.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem:
Is this an opportunity or a pitfall of digital media?

Residents organise an online petition for safer school crossings.
questions.explain: Civic participation: an opportunity.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem:
Is this an opportunity or a pitfall of digital media?

A teenager's home address is posted in a group chat to encourage people to confront him.
questions.explain: Doxxing: a pitfall.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem:
Is this an opportunity or a pitfall of digital media?

A Phagwah livestream from Guyana is watched by Guyanese in New York and Toronto.
questions.explain: Culture and heritage reaching the diaspora: an opportunity.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem:
Is this an opportunity or a pitfall of digital media?

A cropped screenshot makes a teacher's message look rude and is shared across the island.
questions.explain: Edited or cropped content: a misread message.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem:
Is this an opportunity or a pitfall of digital media?

Older workers lose shifts when a business moves bookings online and offers them no training.
questions.explain: Near-term inequality: a pitfall.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem:
The activity: how could each message be misread, and what should the producer do before publishing?

A carnival troupe posts "Our rivals' costumes this year... wow." with no picture.
options: Add context or rewrite it so it cannot be read as sarcasm
questions.explain: Lost tone: "wow" can read as praise or mockery. Say what you mean.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem: A health campaign uses a hand gesture that is friendly in one culture but rude in another.
options: Test the graphic with people from different backgrounds first
questions.explain: Ambiguous visuals: testing with a varied audience catches the problem before launch.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem: A news page wants to share a screenshot of one sentence from a minister's long speech.
options: Link to or quote the full context with the screenshot
Crop it tightly so it fits a story
questions.explain: Edited or cropped content strips meaning. Give the full context.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem: A student messages a group project partner: "Great job finishing it the night before. Again."
options: Send it, the partner will understand
Rephrase directly and kindly, or say it face to face
questions.explain: Sarcasm in short texts is easily misread and can damage relationships.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem:
You run the social media page for the Freeport Youth Sports League in Grand Bahama. It is the night of the under-15 final. Use the four questions: who benefits, who is harmed, who is left out, and what if it is kept forever?

A parent sends you a funny video of a 13-year-old player crying and slipping in the mud after a missed penalty. It would go viral. What do you do?
options: Post it: it will bring the page thousands of followers.
Do not post it. Share the team celebration photo instead, taken with consent.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem: You want to post the results tonight. Many families in the league have limited data and some parents speak mainly Spanish. How do you post?
options: A short captioned image of the scores in English and Spanish, with a low-data link to the highlights.

questions.topic: Opportunities, risks and AI in digital media
questions.stem: A comment appears under the post sharing the referee's home address and telling people to "visit him". What now?
options: Leave it up. It is only a comment and it brings engagement.
Hide and report the comment, save evidence, inform the league and post a reminder of the page's respect rules.

questions.stem: The Seagrape Cove Resort in Negril needs one image for its website, social media, brochures and email newsletters for the next three years, at the lowest total cost. Which licensing option is MOST suitable?
options: No licence, because a resort is allowed fair dealing for advertising.
A rights-managed licence, because it is always cheaper for long-term use.
Any image from a search engine, because online images are public domain.
A royalty-free licence, because a one-time fee covers many uses within the licence terms.

questions.stem:
Your CAPE Digital Media SBA video is due in three days. You are short on time and money. Make the best decisions.

Your laptop's trial of a paid video editor has expired. A friend sends you a link to a cracked version. What do you do?
options: Install the cracked version; everyone does it.
Install a free, open-source editor such as Shotcut or OpenShot instead.

questions.stem: You want a soundtrack. Your favourite chart song would be perfect. What do you use?
options: The chart song; it is only for school.
A Creative Commons or royalty-free track whose licence allows your use, credited in the end titles.

questions.stem: You filmed classmates at a school event. One asks not to appear. You also used an AI tool to draft your narration. What do you do?
options: Keep the footage and say nothing about AI.
Remove or blur that classmate, and state in your portfolio that AI helped draft the narration, which you then rewrote.

questions.stem:
You are the team's project manager. The deadline is Friday. Make a justified decision about each student's plan.

Malik says, "The commercial song is perfect, and the YouTube clip shows the damage better than anything we could film. It's for school, so it's fine." What do you decide?
options: Keep both. Nobody checks school projects.
Replace the song with CC BY music (credited) and email the broadcaster for permission, using the team's own footage if there is no reply.

questions.stem: Maya has found powerful survivor photos by a local photographer and wants to caption them with full names. What do you decide?
options: Post the photos with names now and remove them later if anyone complains.
Ask the photographer for a licence and credit them; contact the survivors for consent and leave names out for anyone who does not agree.

questions.stem: Jerome has changed the colours of a famous logo for the project's brand. What do you decide?
options: Ask him to design an original logo in Inkscape, linked to the project's theme of rebuilding.
Keep it. Changing the colours makes it a new design.

Design separate apps for each age group.
Offer clear labels, a step-by-step guided mode and fast biometric login.
Keep the old paper forms and add a PDF download.

questions.stem: Someone opens a fake account using a student's name and photos.

questions.stem: A false health rumour spreads through WhatsApp groups and frightens younger users.
questions.explain: Freedom from misinformation falls under safety. Literacy is the skill that helps users resist it.

questions.stem: Mrs. Hodge, aged 57, runs a guest house in Saba. She now takes bookings by email and a booking website, but she still prints every reservation and confirms large bookings by phone. Which description fits her BEST?
options: A digital immigrant who adapts skills from pre-digital experience.
Neither, because the labels only apply to young people.
A digital immigrant who refuses to use technology.
A digital native, because she uses a booking website.

Publish all forms as printable PDFs.

questions.stem:
You run social media for the Trinidad music label Steelpan Sound. A change in one part of the ecosystem ripples across all the others. Make the best decisions as three changes hit.

Change 1: a platform changes its algorithm. Your long horizontal music videos suddenly reach far fewer people, while short vertical clips are being pushed.
options: Keep posting exactly as before; the algorithm will change back.
Cut 30-second vertical clips from each video and link them to the full release.

questions.stem: Change 2: a regulator introduces a new data protection rule. You must get clear consent before adding fans to your email list.
options: Keep importing phone contacts from event ticket sales without asking.
Update the sign-up form with a clear consent box and a short privacy notice.

questions.stem: Change 3: an advertiser wants proof. A drinks brand will sponsor your Carnival series only if you show who watches and for how long.
options: Use your analytics systems to report views, watch time and audience location.
Send screenshots of a few nice comments instead.

questions.stem:
You manage releases at the Pelican Motion studio. A short animated film about Curaçao folklore is ready. Make the best value-chain decisions.

How will you distribute the film?
options: Burn DVDs and sell them only at the studio door.
Upload to a large video platform and also screen it at a local festival, to combine global reach with local buzz.

questions.stem: The film is online. How will you help audiences discover it?
options: Do nothing; good content always finds its audience.
Post short teaser clips, write a clear title and description, and ask partner tourism pages to share it.

questions.stem: After two weeks the analytics show most viewers leave after 40 seconds, and 60% are viewers in the Netherlands. What next?
options: Use the feedback: tighten the opening, add Dutch subtitles and plan the next film with this audience in mind.
Ignore the data; the film is finished.

questions.stem: Why do regional video-sharing platforms in the Caribbean find it hard to compete with the largest global platforms?
options: Caribbean audiences do not watch online video.
It is impossible to build a website in the Caribbean.
Regional platforms are not allowed to show advertising.
Global platforms benefit from network effects: their huge numbers of users attract more creators and advertisers, which attract still more users.
